items.title: Santé oculaire : 407 opérations gratuites de la cataracte réalisées à Lomé
items.description: Lomé, 21 oct. (ATOP) – Quatre cent sept personnes ont été opérées gratuitement de la cataracte dans le cadre de la campagne médicale de soins oculaires menée à Lomé du 15 au 21 octobre. Cette initiative vise à réduire la cécité évitable et à faciliter l’accès aux soins oculaires pour les personnes vulnérables. La campagne est portée par l’ONG Al Wifaq pour le Développement social et culturel au Togo (ADSoC), en partenariat avec l’ONG Al Basar International Foundation, avec l’appui du ministère en charge de la Santé, à travers le Programme national de santé oculaire (PNSO). Dr Prempe (milieu) livrant son allocution Outre les interventions chirurgicales, la campagne a permis de distribuer gratuitement plus de 400 paires de lunettes de lecture et 5 000 médicaments aux personnes dans le besoin. Ces prestations visent à soulager les troubles visuels et à améliorer l’accès aux soins spécialisés pour les populations vulnérables. Le coordonnateur du PNSO, Dr Sefofo Yawo Prempe, a rappelé que, selon une enquête menée en 2024, la cataracte demeure la première cause de cécité au Togo, avec plus de 170 000 cas recensés. Il a toutefois relevé une progression de la prise en charge chirurgicale, passée d’environ 500 opérations par million d’habitants en 2000 à 1 790 en 2025. Des patients déjà opérés Le directeur général d’Al-Wifaq, Mohamed Adamou, et le responsable de gestion de la Maison du Hadj, Général Mohamed Atcha Titikpina, ont fait savoir que cette campagne permet aux populations de bénéficier de soins sans distinction d’origine sociale ou de confession religieuse. Ils ont souligné l’importance de la solidarité dans l’accès aux services de santé. Après Lomé, la campagne se poursuit dans la région septentrionale. La deuxième phase est prévue du 22 au 28 octobre à Kara, où les populations pourront également bénéficier de consultations et de soins ophtalmologiques gratuits. ATOP/SED/AO/KYA

items.description: The government has directed the Minerals Commission to ensure that workers in Ghana’s mining industry do not suffer reductions in wages, benefits or conditions of service as mining companies transition from owner mining to contract mining. The directive is part of additional policy measures announced by the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources to guide the implementation of Ghana’s contract mining policy while safeguarding workers’ rights and welfare. In a statement signed by the Ministry’s Director of Communications, Zambaga Rufai Saminu, the government said no worker should be disadvantaged by the transition to contract mining. The Ministry said the measures followed concerns raised by the Ghana Mineworkers Union, human resource experts and other stakeholders about the potential impact of the transition on workers’ salaries, wages and conditions of service. “No worker shall be rendered worse off as a consequence of its implementation,” the statement said, adding that contract mining workers should enjoy salaries, wages, allowances, benefits and other incentives equivalent to those of owner mining workers performing comparable work before the transition. Government reinforces local content requirements The Ministry reiterated that indigenous Ghanaian companies are required to undertake contract mining for surface mining operations, while underground contract mining must be carried out through partnerships in which Ghanaian-owned companies hold at least a 50 per cent interest. The requirement was incorporated into the sixth edition of the Local Procurement List, which took effect on January 1, 2025, under the Minerals and Mining (Local Content and Local Participation) Regulations, 2020 (LI 2431). According to the Ministry, most multinational mining companies operating in Ghana have successfully transitioned their operations to comply with the requirement. “The successful transition undertaken by the majority of multinational mining companies demonstrates that the local content requirement is practicable and enjoys broad industry support,” the statement said. It added that the Ministry and the Minerals Commission had held extensive consultations with the leadership of the Ghana Mineworkers Union, industry experts and other relevant stakeholders to address concerns surrounding the policy. The engagements, it said, had clarified the regulatory and policy basis of the directive and reaffirmed the government’s commitment to protecting workers during the transition. Minerals Commission to prevent deterioration in conditions of service Under the new measures, the Minerals Commission has been directed to ensure that no worker engaged, or to be engaged, by a mining contractor or similar service provider suffers any reduction in wages, emoluments, entitlements, benefits or conditions of service as a result of the shift from owner mining to contract mining. The Commission is also expected to take the necessary steps to harmonise salaries, wages and conditions of service across the mining industry value chain. In addition, eligible contractors are to be categorised according to their capacity to provide mining-related services. The Ministry said the measures were supplementary to existing regulatory requirements and would not prevent the Minerals Commission from taking any further lawful action needed to advance the objectives of LI 2431. The Commission has been given until November 30, 2026, to complete the processes required to implement the measures and submit the necessary documents for approval. Government warns against labour abuses and bid rigging The Ministry also warned against practices that could undermine local content objectives or disadvantage Ghanaian workers. It said the government would maintain “ZERO TOLERANCE” for unfair labour practices, cartelisation, bid rigging, fronting and other conduct that undermines genuine Ghanaian participation in the mining industry. “The Government remains resolute in ensuring fairness, transparency, genuine Ghanaian participation and the protection of workers across the mining industry value chain,” the statement said. The Ministry said the measures formed part of the government’s Reset Agenda under President John Dramani Mahama and were intended to ensure that the implementation of the contract mining policy advanced local participation without compromising workers’ welfare.

F.Z El Mansouri explique l’éviction de Madiha Khayr et récuse toute idée de flottement
items.description: La cheffe du gouvernement, Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, a expliqué mercredi devant la Chambre des conseillers les raisons de la révocation de Madiha Khayr, quelques jours après sa nomination au gouvernement. Elle affirme à ce propos que de nouveaux documents et informations ont fait apparaître des soupçons justifiant cette décision, qu’elle présente comme un acte de fermeté plutôt que comme un signe de désorganisation au début du mandat. Intervenant lors de la séance plénière consacrée à la discussion du programme gouvernemental, Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri est revenue sur la décision de mettre fin aux fonctions de Madiha Khayr, qui avait été nommée ministre déléguée chargée de la Formation professionnelle et de la Qualification. La cheffe du gouvernement a expliqué qu’elle ne disposait pas, au moment de la formation de l’Exécutif, d’informations susceptibles de soulever des soupçons concernant la personne concernée, et qui, a-t-elle rappelé, avait été réhabilitée sur le plan judiciaire en 2019. Selon El Mansouri, la consultation de nouveaux documents et informations a ensuite fait apparaître des éléments qui ont suscité des interrogations sur sa capacité à gérer les deniers publics et les intérêts futurs des Marocains. C’est sur la base de ces éléments qu’elle affirme avoir décidé de demander la révocation de la ministre. La cheffe du gouvernement a indiqué avoir soumis sa demande au Roi Mohammed VI, qui y a répondu rapidement. Elle a défendu cette démarche face aux critiques présentant cette séquence comme un signe de flottement ou d’improvisation au démarrage de la nouvelle équipe gouvernementale. Pour El Mansouri, la décision traduit au contraire la volonté d’agir dès l’apparition d’éléments jugés préoccupants. Elle a affirmé que son gouvernement ne tolérerait pas les situations entourées de soupçons, tout en rejetant ce qu’elle a qualifié de campagnes de déstabilisation, de propos infondés et de rumeurs. Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri a également réagi aux critiques visant un ministre exerçant une activité dans le secteur de l’industrie automobile, auxquelles certains ont associé un possible conflit d’intérêts. Elle s’est interrogée sur le lien établi entre son activité d’entrepreneur et les fonctions ministérielles qu’il exerce aujourd’hui. Selon elle, le responsable concerné contribue à attirer des investissements dans le pays. La cheffe du gouvernement a rappelé qu’en 2017, avant d’occuper une fonction ministérielle, celui-ci était un jeune investisseur qui avait eu recours au financement bancaire et pris des risques pour concrétiser son projet. La cheffe du gouvernement a conclu en réaffirmant que son équipe ne tolérerait pas les soupçons, mais qu’elle n’accepterait pas non plus les attaques et les campagnes qu’elle juge infondées. The post F.Z El Mansouri explique l’éviction de Madiha Khayr et récuse toute idée de flottement appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Egypt entering Yemen war makes situation ‘more difficult’ – Iran
items.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said that any interference in the Yemen war by Egypt or any other country would make the situation “more difficult”. “Egypt has sufficient experience to avoid entangling itself in such a highly complex conflict,” said Iran’s top diplomat in an interview with Iraqi state broadcaster Al-Iraqiya aired on Tuesday. “We believe that any foreign presence or interference will only make resolving this issue more difficult,” Araghchi noted. He added that Egypt has said it “will not enter Yemen or engage in a war against Yemen”. The decade-plus war between the Iran-backed Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen’s internationally recognised government reignited in July. The Houthis seized much of Yemen’s Red Sea coastline in September and have since launched attacks on Saudi Arabia, including strikes on state oil giant Aramco and Riyadh’s international airport, where 13 people were killed on October 10. Egypt’s parliament on Monday delayed a debate on President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi’s request to authorise military support for Saudi Arabia until next week. Sisi had asked lawmakers to approve military support for Saudi Arabia if requested by the kingdom, which has come under near-daily attacks from Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis. Sisi said Egypt was not seeking to “confront or attack anyone”, adding: “We are speaking only about defence.” AFP The post Egypt entering Yemen war makes situation ‘more difficult’ – Iran appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Delayed HIV test results, misconceptions fuel concerns over stigma in Ghana
items.description: Delays in receiving HIV test results and persistent misconceptions about how the virus spreads are raising concerns about Ghana’s efforts to improve HIV services and tackle stigma against people living with the virus. The concerns emerged at the launch of the Community-Led Monitoring (CLM) initiative for HIV, tuberculosis and malaria services, organised by AngloGold Ashanti (AGAMAL). AGAMAL’s Head of Programmes, Malik Kofi Assan, said the initiative would help identify gaps in healthcare delivery and strengthen accountability in services for the three diseases. He cited the organisation’s first-quarter data analysis, which showed an increase in HIV testing but persistent delays in returning results to clients. “We have done our first-quarter data analysis. There are some key things that are evident. One of them is HIV testing. More people go for testing, but the results do not come early,” he said. Mr Assan said community-led monitoring would allow people to assess the quality of healthcare services, identify challenges and engage relevant authorities to improve service delivery. HIV misconceptions persist Director of Research, Monitoring and Evaluation at the Ghana AIDS Commission, Isaiah Doe Kwao, raised concerns about misinformation surrounding HIV transmission, warning that misconceptions could fuel stigma and discrimination. He said some people wrongly believe that mosquito bites can transmit HIV, while others misunderstand the role of lubricants in preventing infection. “There are still misconceptions about how people get HIV/AIDS. People mistakenly believe that when you use lubrication, it helps prevent HIV/AIDS. People still believe a mosquito bite can give HIV,” he said. Mr Kwao stressed the need for reliable public education to correct such beliefs and protect people living with HIV from discrimination. He clarified that HIV cannot be transmitted through mosquito bites and urged intensified efforts to ensure the public has accurate information about the virus. Lubricants do not, on their own, prevent HIV infection. Their role depends on the type of lubricant and how it is used; HIV prevention requires appropriate measures, including condoms and, where suitable, pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP). Communities to monitor healthcare services The Community-Led Monitoring initiative is expected to empower communities to identify gaps in HIV, tuberculosis and malaria services and engage service providers and relevant authorities to address them. It also aims to improve accountability and ensure that people accessing care receive timely, quality and responsive healthcare. The concerns raised at the launch highlight the importance of addressing both weaknesses in service delivery and misinformation as part of efforts to improve health outcomes and reduce stigma against people living with HIV.

items.title: Translog Africa 2026 : La logistique et l’intelligence économique au cœur de l’industrialisation africaine
items.description: La 5ᵉ édition du Symposium international sur le transport et la logistique (Translog Africa) s’est poursuivie ce mercredi 21 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou avec plusieurs panels consacrés aux défis du secteur. À travers le panel III, placé sous le thème « Industrialisation, financement des infrastructures logistiques et intelligence économique », trois experts ont mis en lumière les leviers nécessaires pour renforcer les infrastructures, mobiliser les financements et améliorer la compétitivité des économies africaines. La logistique, le financement des infrastructures et la maîtrise de l’information constituent des leviers essentiels pour accélérer l’industrialisation du continent. C’est le principal communications présentées lors du panel III de Translog Africa 2026. La présentation Intervenant sur le sous-thème « Logistique et industrialisation en Afrique : quel rôle pour les acteurs du transport et de la supply chain ? », Nazaire Moko Mbota, cadre en administration des affaires et en sciences économiques, directeur chargé des missions à l’OGEFREM, a souligné l’importance stratégique de la logistique dans le développement industriel. Selon lui, la dépendance à plusieurs corridors régionaux, les coûts élevés du transport, les retards aux frontières et les insuffisances en matière de traçabilité constituent des obstacles à la compétitivité. Une vue des participants Nazaire Moko Mbota a ainsi rappelé qu’une usine performante ne suffit pas à garantir une production efficace si les matières premières arrivent tardivement ou si les chaînes d’approvisionnement sont perturbées. Pour renforcer cette dynamique, il a mis en avant la complémentarité entre les acteurs du transport, chargés d’assurer la circulation fiable des marchandises, et ceux de la supply chain, responsables de la planification et de la coordination des flux. Nazaire Moko Mbota, cadre en administration des affaires et en sciences économiques, directeur chargé des missions à l’OGEFREM, a souligné l’importance stratégique de la logistique De son côté, Augustin Karanga, économiste des transports et consultant, a abordé la question de la gouvernance, du financement et des partenariats nécessaires au développement des infrastructures logistiques. Il a notamment insisté sur le rôle des plateformes logistiques dans le transit, le tri et la redistribution des marchandises. Pour l’économiste des transports et consultant situées à proximité des grands axes de transport, elles favorisent l’intermodalité, accélèrent les livraisons et contribuent à réduire la congestion routière ainsi que les émissions de CO₂. Toutefois, leur développement reste confronté à plusieurs contraintes, notamment l’insuffisance des infrastructures, la faiblesse des financements et la lenteur des procédures douanières. Face à ces défis, le consultant a préconisé une meilleure préparation des projets, le renforcement de leur viabilité financière et la coordination des bailleurs de fonds. Il a également plaidé pour la digitalisation des procédures et la mise en place de guichets uniques afin de fluidifier les opérations sur les corridors. Augustin Karanga, économiste des transports et consultant Le Dr Honoré Ouédraogo, enseignant-chercheur, expert en intelligence économique et stratégie et directeur général de Burkina Compétitivité SARL, a mis l’accent sur la veille stratégique. Il a présenté l’intelligence économique comme une démarche de collecte, de maîtrise et d’exploitation de l’information au service de la décision. Selon, le Dr Honoré Ouédraogo, dans le domaine logistique, cette maîtrise permet d’anticiper les risques, de limiter les pertes et de réduire les coûts. À l’inverse, une mauvaise gestion de l’information peut compromettre l’efficacité des opérations. Pour l’expert, l’enjeu consiste donc à transformer les données disponibles en connaissances utiles, puis en décisions et en actions concrètes. Dr Honoré Ouédraogo, enseignant-chercheur, expert en intelligence économique et stratégie et directeur général de Burkina Compétitivité SARL Ces échanges ont mis en évidence la nécessité d’associer infrastructures adaptées, financements efficaces, coordination des acteurs et maîtrise de l’information pour faire de la logistique un moteur de l’industrialisation et de la compétitivité en Afrique. Lire aussi : Translog Africa 2026 : La résilience et la sécurisation des chaînes logistiques au centre des réflexions Sakinatou ZOUNDI Minute.bf

items.title: Le 13ème Salon international de l’agriculture et de l’agroalimentaire de Lomé lancé
items.description: Lomé, 21 oct. (ATOP) – Le 13 eme Salon international de l’agriculture et de l’agroalimentaire de Lomé (SIALO), couplé de la 3 ème exposition élevage et de la 3 ème conférence de Gestion de l’environnement et la protection de la création (GIPC), a été lancé le mardi 20 octobre à Lomé. Le SIALO qui se déroule du 20 au 25 octobre, constitue une plateforme de valorisation des potentialités agricoles et animales, de promotion des produits locaux et de rapprochement des acteurs des chaînes de valeur. Il favorise les échanges commerciaux, le partage d’expériences, la présentation d’innovations et la création de partenariats. Producteurs, éleveurs, transformateurs, distributeurs, chercheurs et investisseurs peuvent ainsi faire connaître leur savoir-faire, développer leur réseau professionnel et exploiter de nouveaux horizons. M. Bouab (au micro) Ce salon permettra aux acteurs du secteur agricole du Togo, du Bénin, du Mali et d’ailleurs, d’accroître leur visibilité auprès des visiteurs professionnels et le grand public ; de partager des expériences avec les professionnels ; de développer des relations d’affaires ; de rechercher des débouchés internationaux et de trouver des opportunités de financement, entre autres. Cette édition est placée sous le thème : « Production agricole et animale face au changement climatique : défis et opportunités pour un système alimentaire durable en Afrique ». Ce choix revêt des enjeux majeurs, notamment en termes de la rareté des pluies, des sécheresses, des inondations, de la dégradation des terres et des difficultés d’accès à l’eau qui fragilisent les productions, les revenus des exploitants et la disponibilité des aliments. Face à ces défis, le SIALO se donne comme objectifs de promouvoir des pratiques agricoles adaptées, la gestion durable des terres et de l’eau, des semences de qualité, la restauration de la fertilité des sols et des systèmes d’élevage peu résilients. Il est également question de renforcer la recherche d’innovation technologique et l’accès à l’information climatique, le financement des exploitations et la transformation locale des produits agricoles et animals. Ce salon constitue une opportunité d’échange pour l’émergence de solutions concrètes qui permettront d’améliorer la productivité, renforcer la résilience des producteurs et des éleveurs, et contribuer ainsi à des systèmes alimentaires durables capables d’assurer l’accès régulier à une alimentation suffisante et de qualité. C’est également une occasion de mettre en valeur le savoir-faire des éleveurs, la créativité des transformateurs et le potentiel entrepreneurial des jeunes et des femmes. L’édition 2026 de ce salon sera marquée par la 3 ème exposition élevage, qui a pour objectif de promouvoir la disponibilité et l’accessibilité des produits carnés et halieutiques d’origine locale. Il est aussi prévu la 3 ème conférence de la GIPC avec le partenaire stratégique Compassion International. Le directeur de l’entrepreneuriat et du financement agricole, représentant le ministre en charge de l’Agriculture, Bouab Alexandre, a déclaré qu’en quelques années, le SIALO s’est imposé comme un espace privilégié de rencontres et de dialogue, de promotion des investissements et de valorisation des produits nationaux et régionaux. Il a fait savoir que le changement climatique, constitue un défi majeur auquel le secteur agricole fait face de nos jours. Face aux effets néfastes de ce phénomène, a-t-il relevé, le gouvernement a mis en place des stratégies d’adaptation agricole, des technologies résilientes aux variabilités climatiques. Le commissaire général du SIALO, Heatson Tito Attikpo a appelé à encourager une agriculture intelligente, capable d’optimiser l’utilisation des ressources disponibles, de s’adapter au changement climatique, d’améliorer les rendements et de répondre aux exigences croissantes des marchés. Il a invité la population à venir découvrir les produits agricoles exposés et à échanger avec les exposants. ATOP/KYA/BA

items.title: Kadiogo : Le Gouverneur alerte sur la hausse des cas probables de dengue
items.description: Le Gouverneur de la région du Kadiogo, Abdoulaye Bassinga, a informé l'ensemble des populations qu'une augmentation des cas probables de dengue a été observée ces dernières semaines dans la région. Il a, par conséquent, appelé, ce 21 octobre 2026, les populations à renforcer les mesures de prévention contre cette maladie. Le Gouverneur de la région du Kadiogo a invité les populations à porter des vêtements longs, à utiliser des produits répulsifs, à recourir aux moustiquaires imprégnées et à détruire les gîtes larvaires des moustiques, lors des moments de détente et des activités dans les espaces publics. Il a également invité les populations à protéger leurs habitations contre les moustiques. Par ailleurs, le Gouverneur a exhorté les citoyens à se rendre dans un centre de santé en cas de problème de santé et à éviter l'automédication, qui pourrait entraîner des complications. Il a appelé enfin à la vigilance et à la responsabilité collective pour lutter efficacement contre cette maladie. Minute.bf

items.title: LHC moved for release of Imran's sisters as 30-day detention period ends
items.description: LAHORE: The son of Aleema Khan, detained sister of jailed PTI founder Imran Khan, moved the Lahore High Court (LHC) on Wednesday, seeking the production and release of his mother, as well as two aunts. All three of Imran’s sisters — Aleema, Noreen Niazi and Uzma Khan — were detained by authorities in September, under the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, 1960, as the PTI geared up of for a planned protest march towards Islamabad. Their detention was ordered for 30 days. Aleema’s son, Shahrez Khan, filed a fresh plea challenging their detention in the LHC on Wednesday. The petition stated that Imran’s sisters remained at Lahore’s Kot Lakhpat jail despite the lapse of the 30-day period of their detention. The Punjab home secretary (grievance redressal commissioner), the inspector general of police, the Lahore capital city police officer and the Kot Lakhpat jail superintendent have been named as respondents. The petition, filed through Advocate Rana Mudassar Umar, said the sisters’ detention orders were issued on Sept 20 and expired on Oct 19, yet the jail authorities had not released them despite requests. “Therefore, detention of the detenues is against the law and fundamental rights of the individuals,” it contended. The plea further said that the three sisters were not wanted in any case, and raised concerns that they may be implicated in “false criminal cases” if not released. The petition argued that their detention was a consequence of their efforts for their brother’s release. It further contended that the preventive detention could not replace ordinary criminal law, and that the order violated Article 10 as well as the safeguards of Section 3 of the MPO. The petitioner requested the court to direct the jail superintendent to produce the detainees before the court and “set them at liberty, in the interest of justice, equity and fair play”. He asked the court to declare the detention orders void and issue directives for the detainees’ release, while suspending the operation of the orders. The petition has been fixed for Thursday before Justice Abher Gul Khan.

items.title: FDA shuts down Arcan Bitters factory again over illegal production
items.description: The Food and Drugs Authority (FDA) in the Ashanti region, has shut down a second factory belonging to Unni Associates Company Limited, manufacturers of Arcan Bitters, after the company allegedly resumed production despite an earlier closure order. The latest shutdown at Senfi in the Bekwai Municipality follows the closure of the company’s factory at Parkoso in the Asokore Mampong Municipality in September, after laboratory tests detected an undeclared prescription drug in the alcoholic beverage. FDA officials said the company had relocated its operations and continued manufacturing Arcan Bitters without the Authority’s knowledge, prompting another enforcement action. The Authority had earlier ordered the recall of the product from the Ghanaian market after laboratory analysis established the presence of Sildenafil Citrate, a prescription medicine used to treat erectile dysfunction and pulmonary arterial hypertension. The Ashanti Regional Head of the FDA, Dr. Ashraf Haruna, said the discovery of the substance in a beverage registered as an alcoholic food product posed serious health and safety concerns. He said Arcan Bitters, which contains 35 per cent alcohol, was not permitted to contain any medicinal substances. Sildenafil Citrate is a Phosphodiesterase Type 5 inhibitor, and its undeclared presence in an alcoholic drink could expose consumers to potentially harmful effects. During the latest operation, FDA officers locked up the Senfi facility and pasted caution notices at its entrances. The Authority also secured 23 barrels of alcoholic content intended for production, about 1,500 boxes of the beverage, more than 5,000 empty bottles and other manufacturing materials. Dr. Haruna said the FDA was liaising with the police to facilitate the arrest of the factory owner. The Authority has urged the public to refrain from purchasing or consuming Arcan Bitters and called on retailers and distributors to cooperate with efforts to remove the product from circulation.

items.title: Poor Network: Reps give MTN, Airtel, Glo, Mafab seven days
items.description: By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja The House of Representatives Ad Hoc Committee investigating the persistent poor quality of telecommunications services in Nigeria has given the chief executive officers of MTN, Airtel, Globacom, Mafab Communications and other operators seven days to appear before it. The committee directed the telecom executives to appear on October 28, 2026, to explain the persistent deterioration in network quality and their failure to honour previous invitations. The ultimatum was issued at a public hearing in Abuja on Wednesday following the adoption of two motions sponsored by Reps. Sunday Umeha and Afam Ogene. The lawmakers expressed displeasure over the failure of invited operators, including MTN Nigeria and Mafab Communications, to appear before the committee as previously requested. Consequently, the committee directed the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) to ensure that all affected operators comply with the invitation and appear at 2 p.m. on October 28 at Hearing Room 447 of the New Building of the National Assembly Complex, Abuja. The operators were also directed to submit all relevant documents to the committee on or before the scheduled date and explain the factors responsible for the persistent decline in service quality affecting millions of subscribers and businesses nationwide. The lawmakers warned that any chief executive who failed to honour the invitation could face a possible arrest summons to compel their appearance. Speaking at the hearing, the committee chairman, Rep. Olumide Osoba (APC, Ogun), said reliable telecommunications services had become critical to Nigeria’s economy, extending beyond voice calls and internet access to essential commercial activities, including Point of Sale (POS) transactions. Osoba noted that businesses, financial transactions and other essential services depended heavily on reliable telecommunications networks, making recurring service disruptions a matter of serious national concern. He said the House constituted the ad hoc committee to investigate persistent complaints by subscribers and establish the factors responsible for the poor quality of services provided by telecommunications operators. The chairman, however, expressed concern that the invited chief executives had continued to avoid direct engagement with the committee by offering various excuses or sending lower-ranking officials to represent them. He stressed that the committee expected the chief executives to appear personally, noting that they were better positioned to explain their companies’ operational challenges and commitments to improving service delivery. Also speaking, Rep. Ibe Osonwa criticised the operators for what he described as disregard for the House, despite the substantial revenue they generated from their operations in Nigeria. Osonwa said it was unacceptable for companies benefiting from the Nigerian market to ignore legislative invitations, particularly when lawmakers sought explanations on issues directly affecting their customers and the wider economy. He maintained that telecommunications operators had a responsibility to account for the quality of services delivered to Nigerians, warning that the House would not overlook attempts to frustrate its investigation. In his ruling, Osoba urged the NCC to ensure full compliance with the committee’s directive, reiterating that the affected operators must appear on October 28 with the required documents and explanations on the state of their networks. La République du Congo, premier pays africain à coter ses obligations souveraines au Nasdaq Dubai
items.description: Le ministre congolais des Finances, du Budget et du Portefeuille public, Christian Yoka, a sonne, le 19 octobre, la cloche du Nasdaq Dubai, lors d'une ceremonie organisee a l'invitation de Hamed Ali, directeur general de cette place financiere du Golfe, marquant l'entree en cotation des obligations souveraines congolaises. Selon un communique publie par son ministere, le gouvernement congolais a fait admettre a la cote deux emprunts souverains existants, d'un montant total de 1,55 milliard de dollars, deja cotes a la Bourse de Londres. Par cette operation, la Republique du Congo devient le premier etat africain a faire coter ses obligations souveraines au Nasdaq Dubai, offrant ainsi a ses titres une nouvelle place de negociation au Moyen-Orient. « Cette double cotation ne cree aucune dette supplementaire. Elle permet simplement a un plus grand nombre d'investisseurs d'acheter ou de revendre ces titres », a precise le ministere. Selon la meme source, le gouvernement congolais a engage, des 2025, une strategie de restructuration de sa dette. Confronte a d'importantes echeances de remboursement a court terme, le pays a progressivement renoue avec les marches internationaux afin de remplacer une partie de ses engagements par des emprunts a plus long terme, sous l'impulsion du ministre Christian Yoka. Un taux d'interet annuel de 9,5 % « En fevrier, alors que le Congo recherchait 700 millions, les investisseurs etaient prets a apporter plus de 2 milliards, a des conditions d'emprunt de plus en plus favorables », a indique le ministere, precisant que le pays avait mobilise pres de 2,5 milliards de dollars en sept mois. En elargissant sa base d'investisseurs aux pays du Golfe, la Republique du Congo entend ainsi faciliter son acces aux financements internationaux. Dans le detail, la premiere obligation, d'un montant de 700 millions de dollars, a ete emise en fevrier 2026 et arrivera a echeance le 17 fevrier 2035. La seconde, d'une valeur de 850 millions de dollars, a ete emise en mai 2026 et arrivera a echeance le 26 mai 2036. Les deux emissions sont assorties d'un taux d'interet nominal annuel de 9,5 % et prevoient un remboursement progressif du capital. Selon une analyse du site d'information financiere Sika Finance, la cotation a Dubaï ne reduit pas directement la dette congolaise, mais permet de diversifier la base d'investisseurs. Elle pourrait ainsi stimuler la demande de titres souverains congolais sur le marche secondaire et renforcer leur attractivite. Une meilleure perception de ces obligations pourrait, a terme, ameliorer les conditions des futurs emprunts du pays. Cette perspective demeure toutefois tributaire de l'evolution du risque souverain congolais et de l'appetit des investisseurs pour sa dette.

items.title: Audience à l’Assemblée nationale : Le président Selom Klassou échange avec le directeur pays de l’ONUSIDA sur les défis de la riposte au Togo
items.description: Lomé, 21 oct. (ATOP) – Le président de l’Assemblée nationale, Prof. Komi Selom Klassou, et le directeur pays de l’ONUSIDA pour le Togo, la Côte d’Ivoire et le Bénin, Dr Christian Mouala, ont échangé, le mercredi 21 octobre à Lomé, sur les progrès et les défis de la lutte contre le VIH/Sida au Togo. Les discussions ont notamment porté sur la contribution des parlementaires à l’atteinte de l’objectif de mettre fin au Sida comme problème de santé publique d’ici à 2030. Cette rencontre s’inscrit dans le cadre de la visite officielle du Dr Christian Mouala au Togo, du 20 au 25 octobre. Elle a permis de faire le point sur la coopération entre le pays et le Programme commun des Nations Unies sur le VIH/Sida (ONUSIDA), notamment en matière de prévention, de dépistage et de prise en charge des personnes vivant avec le VIH. Au cours des échanges, le responsable de l’ONUSIDA a présenté les avancées enregistrées par le Togo dans la riposte à la maladie. Selon les chiffres communiqués lors de l’audience, 94 % des personnes vivant avec le VIH connaissent leur statut sérologique, 93 % sont sous traitement antirétroviral et 85 % ont atteint la suppression virale. Malgré ces résultats, des efforts restent nécessaires, particulièrement pour prévenir la transmission du VIH de la mère à l’enfant et renforcer les actions de sensibilisation auprès des jeunes de 15 à 24 ans. Les discussions ont également mis l’accent sur la place des parlementaires dans la lutte contre le VIH/Sida. A travers leurs missions de législation, de contrôle de l’action gouvernementale et d’examen du budget, les élus peuvent contribuer à renforcer les politiques de santé, à améliorer le financement des programmes de lutte contre le VIH et à promouvoir l’accès aux services de prévention et de traitement. Dans cette perspective, l’ONUSIDA envisage d’accompagner les parlementaires togolais dans le renforcement de leurs capacités sur les questions liées au VIH et à la santé en général. Cette démarche vise à favoriser une meilleure prise en compte de ces enjeux dans les décisions publiques et à soutenir des politiques inclusives respectueuses des droits humains. Dr Christian Mouala a salué l’engagement des parlementaires togolais ainsi que la qualité des échanges avec le président de l’Assemblée nationale. Il a également souligné la contribution du Togo aux initiatives régionales et internationales de lutte contre le VIH/Sida. Fort de plus de 25 ans d’expérience dans le développement international et la diplomatie sanitaire, dont plus de 15 ans consacrés à la lutte contre le VIH/Sida au sein de l’ONUSIDA, Dr Christian Mouala coordonne les programmes de l’organisation au Togo, en Côte d’Ivoire et au Bénin depuis son bureau multipays basé à Abidjan. La délégation de l’Assemblée nationale comprenait outre le président Klassou, notamment la première vice-présidente, Memounatou Ibrahima, le quatrième vice-président, Ayao Dzreke, le président de la Commission de la santé, Dametoti Kombate, et la vice-présidente de cette commission, Jacqueline Aka. ATOP/IS/AO

items.title: Le Nigeria confirme un premier cas d’Ebola dans la capitale Abuja
items.description: Le Nigeria a confirme, le 20 octobre, un premier cas importe de maladie a virus Ebola de souche Bundibugyo dans sa capitale, Abuja. Selon un communique du ministere federal de la Sante et des Affaires sociales, relaye par l'Organisation mondiale de la sante (OMS), la patiente, recemment arrivee d'Ouganda a bord d'un vol international, a developpe les premiers symptomes le 7 octobre, avant d'etre admise, le 11 octobre, dans un etablissement de sante prive d'Abuja. Le diagnostic a ete confirme le 20 octobre, apres plusieurs jours de prise en charge. L'etat de la patiente se serait depuis aggrave, jusqu'a une « defaillance multiviscerale », selon un responsable sanitaire nigerian. Le 21 octobre, a l'issue d'une reunion d'urgence, les autorites sanitaires ont confirme que l'infection etait due au virus Bundibugyo, apres trois series d'analyses moleculaires. Cette precision a ete apportee par Olajumoke Babatunde, responsable des services de laboratoire de sante publique au Centre nigerian de controle et de prevention des maladies (NCDC). Selon plusieurs medias, la patiente serait une diplomate ayant rejoint Abuja a bord d'un vol en provenance d'Ouganda. Le Nigeria devient ainsi le cinquieme pays a detecter le virus depuis le debut de l'epidemie en Republique democratique du Congo (RDC), apres l'Ouganda, le Kenya et la France. Quarante-quatre personnes contacts identifiees Selon l'OMS, 44 personnes ayant ete en contact avec la patiente ont ete identifiees au Nigeria. Les autorites sanitaires poursuivent leurs investigations pour retrouver et surveiller les personnes susceptibles d'avoir ete exposees au virus, notamment les professionnels de sante, les patients, les accompagnants et les voyageurs ayant cotoye la patiente. Mohamed Janabi, directeur regional de l'OMS pour l'Afrique, a appele les pays a renforcer leur preparation face a la menace epidemique, notamment par une surveillance accrue, des enquetes rapides en cas d'alerte, la mobilisation d'equipes d'intervention et la constitution de stocks suffisants. Il a egalement souligne l'importance d'une detection precoce et d'une reponse rapide et coordonnee pour proteger les professionnels de sante et les populations. L'Ouganda affirme ne compter aucun cas actif Le ministere ougandais de la Sante a indique que la patiente s'etait rendue en Republique democratique du Congo, sans preciser les localites visitees. Les autorites nigerianes n'ont pas encore confirme l'ensemble de son itineraire. Dans un communique publie sur X le 20 octobre, le ministere ougandais a confirme que la patiente avait transite par l'Ouganda sans presenter de symptomes. « Un voyage a travers l'Ouganda ne prouve pas que l'infection a eu lieu ici », a declare le ministere, soulignant que le pays ne comptait aucun cas actif confirme d'Ebola. Le lieu exact de contamination demeure a determiner. L'epidemie continue de faire des victimes en RDC La 17e epidemie d'Ebola en Republique democratique du Congo continue de se propager, touchant desormais huit provinces et 66 zones de sante. Selon les donnees sanitaires arretees au 18 octobre, le pays comptabilisait 9 552 cas confirmes et 4 602 deces depuis le debut de l'epidemie en mai. Au total, 937 patients etaient hospitalises ou places en isolement, tandis que 2 550 personnes avaient gueri. Le taux de letalite s'etablissait a 48,2 %, et 76,9 % des personnes contacts identifiees faisaient l'objet d'un suivi sanitaire. Les violences armees et les deplacements de populations compliquent davantage la reponse sanitaire. L'extension de l'epidemie, conjuguee a la detection de cas importes au Nigeria et au Kenya, renforce les inquietudes quant aux risques de propagation regionale du virus.

items.title: Food Security: Abiodun targets 10,000 farmers with subsidised inputs
items.description: Distributes 10 tractors, 1,200 smartphones to farmers Unveils 39 tractors, harvesters, agro-processing facilities Over 160,000 farmers, value-chain operators captured in state database ByClifford Ndujihe Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun, has stepped up efforts to boost food production, reduce post-harvest losses and improve farmers’ incomes, unveiling a fresh package of subsidised inputs, mechanisation equipment and digital tools targeting 10,000 rice and cassava farmers. The intervention, announced during the 2026 World Food Day celebration in Abeokuta, includes support for 2,000 rice farmers and 8,000 cassava farmers, the distribution of 10 tractors and 1,200 Android phones loaded with agricultural applications. Under the programme, each beneficiary will receive two bags of fertiliser and one bag of urea. Cassava farmers will also get 25 bundles of cassava stems and 10 litres of herbicides each, while rice farmers will receive three litres of herbicides. The state government said beneficiaries would pay 30 per cent of the cost of the inputs, with the government covering the remaining 70 per cent through its partnership with the International Fund for Agricultural Development, IFAD. The initiative is aimed at reducing farmers’ production costs and improving their capacity to increase output amid rising agricultural expenses and concerns over food affordability. Abiodun also disclosed that his administration had procured 39 tractors, four self-propelled harvesters and other agricultural equipment to strengthen mechanised farming across the state. The 1,200 smartphones distributed to farmers are equipped with applications providing weather information, market prices and guidance on improved farming practices. The digital intervention builds on the Ogun State Farmer Information Management System, launched in April 2023. According to the governor, more than 160,000 farmers and agricultural value-chain operators have been captured on the platform. Invests in processing, market access Special Adviser to the governor on Media, Mr Kayode Akinmade, said beyond farm inputs and machinery, the administration is investing in storage, processing and market access to reduce losses and improve returns to farmers. Abiodun said 28 agricultural projects had been completed in the preceding two years across crop production, aquaculture and poultry. They include solar dryers, warehouses, cassava processing centres and a poultry processing plant at Ajegunle Farm Settlement in Odeda Local Government Area. The poultry facility, according to the governor, has the capacity to process 5,000 birds daily, or about 1.3 million annually. Under the Ogun State Economic Transformation Project, OGSTEP, agribusiness firms have purchased more than 283,000 tonnes of agricultural produce, while farmer clusters have received capacity-building support and links to off-takers. The government has also partnered with Soilless Farm Lab to train more than 200 young people in soilless farming and provide start-up support to beneficiaries. Abiodun said the Ogun State Agricultural Land Management Agency was established to facilitate access to agricultural land and promote investment in commercial farming. Speaking at the event, a former Deputy Vice-Chancellor of the Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta, Professor Kolawole Adebayo, said Ogun had approximately 1.2 million hectares of arable land, offering significant potential for agricultural production and agro-industrial development. Adebayo called for sustained investment in innovation and an integrated transport network linking rail, road, water and air transport to ease the movement of agricultural produce and preserve its quality. The Commissioner for Agriculture and Food Security, Bolu Owotomo, stressed the importance of ensuring access to nutritious and affordable food, calling for greater investment in women and young people through improved access to land, finance, training and technology. Owotomo disclosed that more than 12,000 farmers had benefited from training and agricultural inputs under OGSTEP. The state government said it would continue to complement federal agricultural interventions through farmer support, investment and stronger market linkages. However, the impact of the initiatives will depend on timely distribution of inputs, effective maintenance of equipment, transparent beneficiary selection and improved access to markets. Higher yields, lower production costs, better farmers’ incomes and reduced post-harvest losses will ultimately determine whether the investments translate into sustained food security and more affordable food for consumers. The post Food Security: Abiodun targets 10,000 farmers with subsidised inputs appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Residents, school authorities demand footbridge at Aboabo after van killed 4 pupils
items.description: The death of four schoolchildren at Aboabo in the Asokore Mampong Municipality has reignited urgent calls for the construction of a footbridge on the dual carriage road that has become notorious for fatal accidents. Four pupils of the School of Islamic Studies at Akotosu have died, while three others are receiving medical attention after a Hyundai van crashed into them. The victims, identified as Juraid Mohammed, Anisah Ibrahim, Fati Muniru and Raiyan Faisal, all eight years old, were pronounced dead on arrival at the Manhyia District Hospital. Other victims, Laila Muniru, 12, and Bushira Musapha, five, are in critical condition and have been referred to the Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital for further treatment. Another victim, six-year-old Saisa Bila, is in stable condition and is receiving treatment at the Manhyia District Hospital. All pupils involved in the accident were said to be crossing the road on Tuesday after school when the incident occurred. According to eyewitness accounts, the Hyundai van, which was travelling from the Aboabo Post Office area towards the Airport Roundabout, reportedly lost control while descending a sloping road and veered onto the pavement where the children were waiting to cross. The vehicle subsequently ran into the children, leaving seven of them injured. The tragedy has left the community devastated, with residents, school authorities and local leaders unanimous in their demand for a footbridge to be constructed immediately to save lives. The Headmaster of the School of Islamic Studies, Bawa Abdul-Rahman, described the stretch as a death trap and said only a footbridge can guarantee the safety of pupils. According to him, the sloping nature of the road makes vehicles speed, as many people have been knocked down along that stretch. “The way forward is to liaise with the Municipal Assembly for us to construct a footbridge here because it is not only the students here that are facing that problem. The road has knocked down so many people along that stretch,” he stressed. He revealed that the school management had previously assigned someone to help the children cross the road after closing, but that person was once almost hit by a speeding car. “From that place, it looks like a highway. If you try stopping them, some recalcitrant drivers still find their way, because these people had already crossed the road, but the car still managed to cross to the other side to hit them. So, it is a footbridge that can solve that problem,” he lamented. As an interim measure, the headmaster said management will insist that pupils use the traffic light at the Aboabo Post Office to cross the road, where there is MTTD presence. The headmaster described the tragedy as tough for both teachers and pupils, but said the school management is trying to stay composed to support the affected families. “It is very heartbreaking, but we are taking it cool because we have to compose ourselves before we can console even the families. They are moody, but we will manage to calm them down. As you can see, they are in class, and we have made sure teaching and learning are still going on,” he said. He added that the guidance and counselling unit of the school will provide psychological support to the affected families and pupils. Meanwhile, the Municipal Chief Executive (MCE) for the Asokore Mampong Municipal Assembly, Ben Abdallah Alhassan, during a visit to the injured victims at the hospital and the families of the deceased, said he has officially filed a report on the incident to the Urban Roads authorities for immediate action. He noted that he has requested the Department of Urban Roads to conduct an immediate assessment of that stretch to determine the necessary safety interventions, including the construction of a footbridge, speed ramps and pedestrian crossings. The MCE assured the bereaved families and residents of the Assembly’s commitment to ensure that lasting measures are put in place to prevent such tragedies in the future. The driver is currently in police custody, while the damaged vehicle has been impounded as investigations into the circumstances surrounding the accident continue. The bodies of the four deceased children have been released to their families for burial in accordance with Islamic rites, as the community continues to mourn and demand lasting safety interventions.

items.title: Tourist in South America died from peanut allergy
items.description: A 24-year-old British tourist died from a peanut allergy after eating churros in South America, an inquest has heard. Cornwall Coroner’s Court heard Harry Kitto, from Falmouth, Cornwall, was told by café staff in Buenos Aires, Argentina, the pastry did not contain peanuts when he asked them both in English and Spanish. The inquest heard Kitto suffered an anaphylactic reaction on 30 October 2025 after biting into the food which contained peanuts. The court heard Harry had been travelling around South America with his girlfriend Naomi Pye and had eaten churros in Mexico and Peru without any issues. The inquest concluded his death was accidental. Pye told the court Kitto felt the churro contained nuts and took a tube back to their accommodation, but his lips became swollen and he began to struggle to breathe. She called for emergency help and ran to the accommodation to get an epi-pen (adrenaline epinephrine auto-injector syringe) and injected it into his thigh as an ambulance arrived on the scene and rushed him to hospital. Pye said the pair were given a “firm no” that the churros contained nuts. The inquest heard his heart stopped for about 11 minutes before it was restarted and he was taken into intensive care. Kitto died one-week later from hypoxic brain injury and anaphylactic shock. ‘Immensely strong’ Assistant coroner Emma Hillson was told Kitto’s father and brother later went to the café and ordered the same food, and asked staff if the churros contained peanuts. One waiter said they did not know and another said no. They took the churro for testing at a local laboratory which showed it contained 20mg of peanut protein per kilo, the inquest heard. Kitto’s mother Kerry Burt said her son “suffered a catastrophic allergic reaction to food cross contaminated with peanuts”. She described her son as being “immensely strong, courageous and brave”. Burt added: “For over a week he showed extraordinary strength and determination – the same strength that made everyone who knew him so proud.”

items.title: Milei a Abascal, en una videollamada: “Para mí es un placer patear culos zurdos”
items.description: Aunque no se han encontrado físicamente, Javier Milei y Santiago Abascal se han visto este miércoles a través de una videollamada en la que el líder de Vox le ha agradecido al presidente argentino por su visita y por su discurso cargado de insultos a la izquierda en el Nueva Economía Fórum , y en la que se ha lamentado por no poder recibirlo personalmente. En sendos vídeos difundidos por el equipo del mandatario y por el propio Abascal en X se les ve a ambos hablar en tono de camaradería y llamándose “Javier” y “Santiago” el uno al otro. Mientras a Abascal se le ve dentro de un coche, Milei se encuentra en una oficina de la sede en Madrid de la Fundación Disenso. “Amigo, ¿cómo estás? items.title: Made-in-Ghana products take centre stage at iNTTA exhibition in Cape Coast
items.description: Made-in-Ghana products spanning clothing, cosmetics, food, arts and crafts, herbal medicine and other locally manufactured goods took centre stage at an exhibition organised as part of the sixth Inter Tourism Expo Accra (iNTTA) in Cape Coast. The exhibition brought together businesses and exhibitors showcasing locally produced goods and services, highlighting opportunities to promote Ghanaian brands, expand market access and strengthen the link between tourism and local enterprise. The displays formed part of the three-day expo, which opened at the Ridge Royal Hotel on Wednesday, October 21, and runs until Friday, October 23, 2026. The event is bringing together tourism professionals, investors, policymakers, entrepreneurs and development partners to explore investment opportunities across tourism, agribusiness, trade, digital innovation and hospitality. The exhibition provided a platform for businesses to present their products to participants and potential partners while showcasing the diversity of Ghana’s local industries. From fashion and beauty products to traditional arts, food and herbal preparations, the displays reflected the range of locally made products that could be incorporated into tourism experiences and marketed to visitors. The exhibition also underscored the potential for tourism to support businesses beyond hotels and tourist attractions by creating markets for local manufacturers, artisans, farmers, food processors and other small enterprises. The expo is being held under the theme, “6th Inter Tourism Expo (iNTTA) and the 24-Hour Africa Economy, Agribusiness, Digital Sovereignty and AfCFTA Industrial Acceleration Conference and Investment Programme.” The wider programme includes investment forums, business-to-business engagements and discussions on tourism infrastructure, agribusiness, digital systems and opportunities under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). The exhibition forms part of efforts to strengthen partnerships between tourism and other sectors while creating opportunities for Ghanaian businesses to showcase their products, reach new customers and explore investment opportunities.

items.title: Kéran/santé maternelle et néonatale : Des équipements biomédicaux à la nouvelle maternité du CHP de Kantè
items.description: Kantè, 21 oct. (ATOP) – Le Centre hospitalier préfectoral (CHP) de Kantè a bénéficié d’un don d’équipements biomédicaux destinés à sa nouvelle maternité. La cérémonie de remise s’est déroulée le mardi 20 octobre à Kantè. Visite à une femme en salle de suite d’accouchement Cette activité s’inscrit dans la mise en œuvre de la composante « Construction, réhabilitation et équipement » d’un projet en cours dans dix structures de soins obstétricaux et néonatals d’urgence (SONU), réparties dans sept préfectures de la région de la Kara. L’objectif est de moderniser et de pérenniser les infrastructures hospitalières afin d’améliorer la prise en charge des femmes enceintes, des femmes en âge de procréer, et de contribuer, à terme, à la réduction de la mortalité maternelle et néonatale. D’un coût total de 528 428 035 FCFA, les travaux et équipements destinés au CHP de Kantè comprennent la construction de la maternité et du logement de la sage-femme responsable de ce service, ainsi que la réhabilitation du bloc administratif. Le lot d’équipements comprend notamment des aspirateurs de mucosités pédiatriques, des kits de réanimation du nouveau-né, un détecteur de pouls fœtal et une banque de sang d’une capacité de 150 poches. Vue partielle des équipements biomédicaux réceptionnés La cheffe de la délégation allemande, Mme Anne Rehner, chargée de la coopération économique et du développement avec le Togo, a procédé à la remise symbolique des équipements au préfet de la Kéran, Douti N’Sarma Mabiba. La cérémonie s’est achevée par une visite des locaux de la nouvelle maternité. Plusieurs autorités politiques, administratives, municipales et traditionnelles ont pris part à l’événement. Parmi celles-ci l’ambassadeur de la République fédérale d’Allemagne au Togo, Stefan Anton Messerer, le directeur régional de la santé de la Kara, Dr Sibabe Agoro, et le directeur préfectoral de la santé de la Kéran, Dr Attipoé Yawovi Mawuena. ATOP/PAP/MD/KYA

items.title: Prix de la viande, aucune baisse constatée à Bamako
items.description: Contrairement aux annonces relayees par certains medias, le prix de la viande n'a pas baisse dans les marches de Bamako visites par notre equipe de reportage ce mercredi. L'Association des bouchers du Mali affirme ne pas avoir ete informee d'une telle decision. Les consommateurs, eux, continuent de denoncer des prix juges trop eleves. Du marche de Medina-Coura a celui de Missira, en passant par Badialan, le constat est identique, les prix de la viande restent inchanges. Le kilogramme de viande de mouton se vend a 5 000 F CFA. Celui de viande de bœuf sans os coûte entre 4 500 et 5 000 F CFA, tandis que le kilogramme de viande de bœuf avec os varie entre 4 000 et 4 500 F CFA. Aucune confirmation d'une baisse du cote des bouchers Makan Haidara, charge de communication de l'Association des bouchers du Mali, dit avoir appris par les medias l'existence d'une eventuelle baisse des prix. Il affirme que l'association n'a pas ete informee d'une telle mesure. « On a entendu la rumeur que le gouvernement a baisse le prix de la viande », explique-t-il. Selon lui, lors d'une rencontre avec les autorites, les bouchers avaient propose la reouverture des parcs a betail a l'interieur du pays. Ainsi que la protection des commercants qui approvisionnent Bamako. Ces mesures devaient, selon l'association, faciliter l'approvisionnement de la capitale et contribuer a la baisse des prix. « Seul le marche a betail de Banamba fonctionne actuellement », deplore Makan Haidara. Les consommateurs toujours confrontes aux prix eleves Sur les marches, les menageres ne constatent aucune reduction des tarifs. Au marche de Medine, une cliente rencontree apres ses achats indique avoir depense 3 000 F CFA pour de la viande. « Le kilo de viande de bœuf avec os coûte 4 000 F CFA, contre 5 000 F CFA sans os. Si le prix avait reellement baisse, mon boucher aurait aussi reduit ses tarifs », affirme-t-elle. Une autre cliente du meme marche confirme que les prix restent les memes. « Le kilo de viande sans os coûte toujours 5 000 F CFA et celui avec os, 4 000 F CFA. Peut-etre que les prix ont baisse dans d'autres marches, mais pas chez nous », temoigne-t-elle. Lire aussi : Youwarou : la viande plus chere, le poisson introuvable Au marche de Badialan, une vendeuse de brochettes souligne egalement avoir achete le kilogramme de viande sans os a 5 000 F CFA. a Missira, une autre menagere releve que le kilo de viande de bœuf sans os coûte 5 000 F CFA et celui avec os, 4 500 F CFA. Elle juge ces tarifs toujours eleves. En attendant une eventuelle application d'une mesure de reduction des prix, les consommateurs continuent d'interpeler les autorites pour une baisse effective du prix de la viande. items.title: Australian MP loses both legs after alleged car attack, husband says
items.description: Helen Haines, the Australian MP who was hit by a car in what authorities say was a deliberate attack, has lost both her legs, her husband has confirmed. Phil Haines said the “horrendous incident” caused his wife significant injuries but “her heart and her mind are in good shape”. He added that the “good news in all this is that she’s alive”. The alleged attacker, 43-year-old Brendan Nugent, faces multiple charges and appeared in court for the first time on Wednesday. Nugent was arrested moments after he allegedly drove his Toyota LandCruiser into the independent MP outside her electorate office in the regional town of Wangaratta, about 240km (150miles) northeast of Melbourne. Haines’ “road to recovery will be long and difficult, but we know she is a fighter,” her husband said at a press conference in Melbourne where she is being treated. “She is a determined person who will do her best, with our support and love, to recover. And that is what we hope for.” He thanked hospital staff and people, both in Australia and internationally, who have shown their concern for Haines, and urged those who want to show their support to donate to the Save the Children fund. “Please keep sending Helen your love,” he added. Earlier onWednesday, Nugent appeared at the local court to face three charges: dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally causing serious injury, and causing harm to a Commonwealth public official. Police said more charges may be laid, including attempted murder. Nugent – a local from the nearby town of Tarrawingee and known as an environmental campaigner – remained silent and emotionless during his brief court appearance. He did not apply for bail and is due back in court in February. Court documents show he was also charged with cultivating and possessing cannabis. In court, Nugent’s lawyer said that his client had “mental health concerns” but did not give any further detail. The court also heard that Nugent has a rare neurological condition – idiopathic transverse myelitis – caused by inflammation of the spinal cord. Victoria Police said its investigation, with support from the Australian Federal Police (AFP), remains ongoing and a motive is yet to be established. “His motivation for this – what we allege is a deliberate attack – is very much a centrepiece of the investigation,” said Victoria Police Commissioner Mike Bush. “Our people will continue to explore every element, angle and avenue to work that out. It’s something that, when we work towards it, discover it, we will present in court.” Nugent was not on the radar of police and there was no intelligence of any threat to Haines before the incident, police said. Investigators are also looking into whether drug use or medication played a part in the incident and if there was any personal connection between Nugent and Haines. Nugent’s family earlier put out a statement saying they were long-time friends with Haines, who is the independent MP for the regional seat of Indi in Victoria. They described the apparent attack as “devastating and unfathomable”. The incident occurred on Monday afternoon at around 15.35, local time. Moments after the car hit Haines, bystanders pulled Nugent out of the vehicle and detained him. Jacob and Jackie Evans were among the first on the scene, and said Haines was grateful to them for coming to her aid as she lay severely injured. “Thank you, you lovely people,” is what Haines said to them, according to the Herald Sun. “She was thanking us, it was incredible,” Jackie told Nine’s Today programme. Jacob used a tourniquet he had in a medical kit in his car to help stem the bleeding from one of Haines’s legs. Haines underwent surgery after the incident and lost one of her legs. As of Wednesday morning she has also lost the other leg, her husband Phil told reporters. The community in Wangaratta, as well as the wider political community, are in shock over the incident in a country where political violence is rare. Leaders from across the political spectrum have paid tribute to Haines, who was first elected in 2019 and is well regarded by her peers. Australia’s Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said he had spoken to Haines’s husband several times since the incident. In an interview with the national broadcaster ABC, Albanese said threats to female politicians were marked by a “different form of vilification and aggression” such as threats of rape. There has also been a recent growing trend of threats against “high office holders”, with almost one person a week being charged for such offences, police said. Monday’s incident has sparked debate over the level of security for MPs. Federal police said that individual protection for every one of the country’s 226 federal MPs would require “incredible” levels of staffing. Instead, police assess the need for close personal protection based on a person’s role and the threat environment around them, police said. Australia’s Governor-General Sam Mostyn, who spoke at the same press conference as Haines’ husband, said this was “a moment for us to pause, and to choose to be better”. “We should do what I imagine Helen would be doing if she was not the victim of this terrible attack – reaching out to those who are terribly distressed by what has happened,” she says. “Most importantly, that we learn or re-learn to exercise our muscle of decency.”

items.title: FCT civil servants, artisans back Tinubu
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Workers in the Federal Capital Territory FCT have endorsed President Bola Tinubu for re-election in 2027, pledging to mobilise supporters across the six Area Councils for his second-term bid. The endorsement was announced by the FCT coordinator of Working People United WoPU, Comrade Musa Fadawa, on Wednesday in Abuja. Fadawa described the group as a labour-oriented movement made up of teachers, nurses, drivers, artisans, traders, civil servants, students and private-sector workers. He said the decision followed consultations with members across the territory and other states. According to him, the movement backed Tinubu because of his commitment to workers’ welfare, his engagement with organised labour and his ongoing economic and infrastructural reforms. Fadawa said the president had shown a willingness to engage the Nigeria Labour Congress NLC and the Trade Union Congress TUC through dialogue and negotiations on workers’ welfare. He cited the approval of wage awards and the new national minimum wage as proof that the administration recognises workers’ challenges. The coordinator said Working People United was established to protect workers’ interests and to mobilise support for a government it believes is concerned about their welfare. He added that the movement believes the president deserves another term to consolidate his policies. Fadawa also announced a partnership with the City Boy Movement, particularly its FCT chapter, to intensify grassroots mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections. He said the partnership would take the re-election campaign to markets, motor parks, workplaces, wards and satellite towns across the territory. Fadawa also credited the Tinubu administration and the FCT Minister, Nyesom Wike, for infrastructure development in the territory. He listed road construction and rehabilitation across the six Area Councils, the renewal of Abuja’s city centre, streetlight installations, bridge construction, school renovations and water projects. According to him, the projects have created jobs, improved transportation and boosted commercial activities, to the benefit of drivers, traders and other working residents. On the national economy, Fadawa defended the removal of fuel subsidy and the unification of the exchange rate, describing both as difficult but necessary reforms. He acknowledged the initial hardship they caused but expressed optimism that their benefits would become clearer as the economy stabilises. He also cited the national minimum wage, student loans through the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), infrastructure development, and youth-focused skills and credit programmes as key parts of the administration’s Renewed Hope Agenda. Fadawa said more must be done to reduce inflation, strengthen the naira and improve living conditions for workers and vulnerable Nigerians. He said the 2027 election would give Nigerians the chance to decide whether to sustain the ongoing reforms, arguing that a second term would enable Tinubu to address persistent economic challenges. As part of its mobilisation strategy, Working People United pledged to encourage members nationwide to register to vote, collect their Permanent Voter Cards PVCs and take part in the elections. The movement also promised ward-to-ward, market-to-market and door-to-door campaigns with the City Boy Movement, while countering what it described as misinformation and divisive narratives. Fadawa called on workers, artisans, traders, students and other Nigerians to join the campaign for Tinubu’s re-election, insisting that continuity was necessary to sustain the administration’s reforms. “He listened when others would have ignored. He negotiated when others would have imposed, the administration had given workers a stronger voice in governance. We, the working people, are saying: Let the work continue. Let Renewed Hope continue,” he said. The post FCT civil servants, artisans back Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ebola: NCDC holds emergency meeting to conclude action plans
items.description: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has convened an emergency meeting and commenced coordinated response activities following the Federal Government’s declaration of an Ebola outbreak in the country. The agency disclosed this in a statement posted on its official X page on Wednesday, saying the meeting brought together its leadership and key partners to coordinate the response. “The first Incident Management Meeting was convened on October 21, 2026, after the Honorable Minister’s official outbreak declaration of Ebola in Nigeria, bringing together leadership and key partners to align on response efforts,” the NCDC said. The agency also announced that its Incident Action Plan was being finalised, while response teams had commenced field operations focusing on surveillance, contact tracing and infection prevention. “The Incident Action Plan is being finalized today; NCDC teams are on the ground conducting case management and response activities, prioritising enhanced surveillance, contact tracing, infection prevention and control, and coordinated risk communication,” the statement read. Reaffirming its commitment to containing the outbreak, the agency said, “We remain committed to a timely, coordinated, and evidence-based response to safeguard the health of Nigerians.” The Federal Government confirmed Nigeria’s first Ebola virus disease case on Tuesday after laboratory tests returned positive in the Federal Capital Territory. The patient, a woman who recently travelled from Uganda on an international flight, reportedly received treatment at a private hospital for several days before the infection was confirmed. She has since been placed in isolation. The post Ebola: NCDC holds emergency meeting to conclude action plans appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ebola: Atiku challenges Tinubu to account for N10bn
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged President Bola Tinubu to account for the N10 billion announced for Ebola preparedness, alleging that the confirmed case in Abuja exposed serious gaps in surveillance and the protection of health workers. Atiku said the government must explain how the emergency funds were spent and why the response allegedly left frontline health workers without adequate protective equipment. He also warned against using the outbreak to restrict political campaigns and voter participation. In a statement by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, on Wednesday, Atiku demanded a public audit of the funds and answers over the handling of the case. “Where is the money? Publish the amount actually disbursed, the dates of payment, every contract awarded, every recipient and every item delivered. A press statement cannot replace an audit,” he said. Atiku said the patient arrived in Nigeria on October 5, developed symptoms on October 7 and sought treatment at a private hospital on October 11, but the government did not publicly confirm the case until October 20. “During that critical period, 44 close contacts were left unmonitored, while private health workers faced the case without adequate protective equipment. This is a failure of preparedness with potentially grave consequences,” he said. He also questioned the Presidential Task Force announced by Tinubu in June and chaired by his Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila, insisting that medical experts should lead the response. “Political titles cannot trace contacts, equip hospitals or save lives,” Atiku said. The former vice president further alleged that the planned press conference by the Minister of Health on Thursday was intended to discourage Nigerians from attending campaign rallies and voting. “The Tinubu administration must not weaponise Ebola to frighten the public, silence its opponents or suppress voter participation. Any public health measure must be backed by clear medical evidence, applied equally and never used as a pretext to interfere with Nigerians’ democratic rights,” he said. Atiku urged the government to account for the N10 billion, protect health workers and trace all contacts, warning against turning a public health emergency into a tool for political suppression. The post Ebola: Atiku challenges Tinubu to account for N10bn appeared first on Vanguard News .
