items.title: Nigeria loses ₦1.13tn yearly to foreign cloud dependency — Study
items.description: Experts downplay fears of AI-driven job losses By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — Nigeria loses about $850 million, equivalent to ₦1.13 trillion, annually through its reliance on cloud infrastructure provided by a handful of foreign companies, according to research commissioned by global technology philanthropy Luminate. The Chief Executive Officer of Luminate, Melanie Hui, disclosed this on Wednesday in Abuja while delivering the keynote address at the Build 2026 Conference, convened by the Nigeria Artificial Intelligence (AI) Collective. In her address, titled “Africa in the Global AI Order: Towards Equitable Ownership and Shared Prosperity,” Hui said the country’s dependence on foreign cloud infrastructure raised questions about digital ownership and the distribution of economic value. “Nigeria, like countries across the world, relies heavily on cloud infrastructure provided by a handful of foreign companies. The research we commissioned estimates that this dependency costs Nigeria around $850 million each year,” she said. Hui stressed that hosting digital infrastructure within a country’s borders did not necessarily translate into ownership or control. “A country does not own its digital future when a data centre merely sits within its borders. The more important questions are who controls it, who can afford to use it, what powers it, whose data it processes and where the resulting economic value flows,” she said. She also drew attention to the historical inequalities reflected in Africa’s digital infrastructure, noting that the fibre-optic cables carrying the continent’s internet traffic followed some routes associated with historic injustice. “Infrastructure, indeed, encodes relationships of power. It determines who connects to whom, who controls the gates, who pays rent, and who extracts value,” she said. According to Hui, Africans should not be confined to subordinate roles in the global AI economy. “My African friends tell me they will not be confined to the role of consumer, supplier of raw data, source of critical minerals or provider of low-paid labour in somebody else’s AI economy,” she said. On data governance, she warned against treating people and communities merely as sources of information from which technology companies could generate products and profits. “People and communities must not be treated as reservoirs of data from which others fashion their products, profits and ideas,” she said. Hui also rejected arguments that regulation necessarily slows technological progress, insisting that safeguards were essential to responsible innovation. “Those of us who promote tech justice must not lend credence to some, in the tech industry, who would paint regulation as a brake on progress. I disagree. Safeguards are the allies of progress,” she said. Citing examples of efforts to hold technology companies accountable, she referenced the Nigerian competition authority’s action against Meta over alleged data exploitation and discriminatory practices. She also noted that app-based drivers in Nigeria had secured government recognition for what she described as Africa’s first e-hailing trade union. Hui called for an AI economy rooted in African agency, capabilities and innovation, where prosperity would be measured not only by market size but also by the opportunities and freedoms available to people. Experts Say AI Could Create More Jobs At the conference, technology experts also sought to allay fears that artificial intelligence would lead to widespread job losses, arguing that the technology could create new employment opportunities and improve productivity. Their comments came amid warnings by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank about AI’s potential impact on the global labour market. IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva recently described AI as a “slow-moving tsunami” at the “Small AI: More and Better Jobs” event during the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand. She said about 40 per cent of jobs globally could be augmented, downgraded or eliminated by the technology. World Bank Group President Ajay Banga, meanwhile, has emphasised the need to ensure that development translates into employment, arguing that AI should improve productivity and support job creation rather than simply replace workers. However, the Chief Executive Officer of Data Science Nigeria, Dr Olubayi Adekanmbi, argued that the overall gains from AI could outweigh the losses. “There is something we call net effect. Some wins and some losses. But by the time you weigh them together, you will realise that the net effect of AI is going to be much more. Because many jobs that never existed before, AI will make them possible,” he said. Adekanmbi maintained that human judgement would remain important even as AI tools became increasingly integrated into professional work. “AI can help in my diagnosis, but the final decision will still come from doctors. So, a doctor can reach out to more people faster because the doctor has used AI. It’s never taking the job of a doctor. That is why everybody must learn AI so that when you learn AI with your current job, you will not lose your job,” he said. He urged workers to acquire AI skills and learn how to apply the technology within their existing professions. Digital Skills Key to Job Creation The Executive Director of the Policy Innovation Centre and host of the Nigeria AI Collective Secretariat, Dr Osasuyi Dirisu, said digital skills development would be critical to creating jobs for Nigeria’s young population. “We have a very young demographic in Nigeria. In order to create jobs at scale, we need to leverage digital technology. We need to leverage digital jobs, and one of the ways to do that is to build digital skills,” she said. Dirisu said young Nigerians needed to be prepared for emerging employment opportunities through training and continuous skills development. She described the Nigeria AI Collective as “a community of practice that is working to build an ethical and inclusive future for AI development in Nigeria.” Experts Address AI-Generated Election Falsehoods The conference also examined concerns over the use of AI to spread misinformation, disinformation and deepfakes ahead of the 2027 general elections. Dirisu said the Centre for Journalism Innovation and Development (CJID), a partner of the Collective, was working to address the threat through election-monitoring labs and media training. Adekanmbi, however, said AI tools could also help Nigerians verify information and counter falsehoods. “Somebody posts something, and you ask Grok, ‘Please confirm,’ Grok can immediately crawl the internet for you and confirm it,” he said. He proposed extending such verification services to Nigerians without internet access through telephone-based systems. “They can use maybe a mobile phone to call a number and say that ‘I heard something,’ and immediately they can get a response telling them that what you heard is not true. The technology for that already exists,” he said. The post Nigeria loses ₦1.13tn yearly to foreign cloud dependency — Study appeared first on Vanguard News .

Dakoa Newman calls for accountability, support for Obuasi SHTS abuse victims
items.description: A former Minister for Gender, Children and Social Protection, Dakoa Newman, has condemned the alleged sexual abuse of female students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), calling for thorough investigations, immediate support for affected students and accountability for anyone found culpable. The former minister, in a statement responding to allegations brought to public attention by investigative journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni in the JoyNews documentary Inside the Dreaded Headmaster’s Bungalow , said the claims were deeply distressing and, if established, would represent “a heinous betrayal of the trust that students, parents and the nation place in those responsible for education.” The statement welcomed the headmaster’s removal from duty pending investigations and the referral of the matter to the Criminal Investigation Department of the Ghana Police Service. However, it stressed that these measures should be the beginning of a comprehensive response. It also acknowledged that the headmaster maintains his innocence and that an earlier Ghana Education Service inquiry reportedly did not substantiate the allegations presented to it. “Each allegation must be examined fairly and on its evidence, without prejudging guilt or dismissing students’ accounts,” the statement said, adding that “due process and the protection of students are not competing obligations; both must be upheld.” The former minister called on the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection, education authorities, police and social welfare services to provide counselling, health services, family support and measures to ensure that the students’ education is not disrupted while investigations continue. The statement also urged investigators to establish how previous complaints were handled, including whether any officials failed in their duties, pressured families to withdraw complaints or obstructed efforts to seek help. It said anyone found to have intimidated complainants or knowingly neglected their responsibilities must be held accountable. “Moving staff, private assurances or waiting for public attention to fade are not resolutions,” the statement said. It further called for safe reporting channels outside any chain of authority implicated in a complaint, protection against retaliation for students, parents and staff who speak up, and a review of safeguarding arrangements in schools, particularly boarding institutions. The review, it said, should examine staff-student boundaries, students’ access to staff residences, supervision arrangements, complaint procedures and the referral of serious concerns. It also appealed to political, traditional, religious and community leaders to ensure that personal relationships, political affiliations or social standing do not shield anyone from accountability. “Protecting an institution’s reputation must never take precedence over protecting its students, and no child’s access to protection should depend on her family’s money, influence or courage to withstand public scrutiny,” the statement added. The former minister commended Manasseh Azure Awuni and the JoyNews team, as well as the students, families and staff who have spoken about the allegations, saying their courage must lead to sustained support, credible investigations and safeguards that remain effective beyond the current public attention.

items.title: Ebola: NBMA offers experts to support NCDC
items.description: By Folarin Kehinde The National Biosafety Management Agency (NBMA) has offered to deploy its biosafety experts to support the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) and other relevant response teams following the reported confirmation of an imported case of Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). The Director-General and Chief Executive Officer of NBMA, Dr Fatima Suleiman-Zuntu, said the agency was ready to provide technical expertise, as required, to complement ongoing containment and infection prevention efforts. Suleiman-Zuntu, in a statement issued in Abuja on Wednesday, reaffirmed the agency’s commitment to supporting the national response through its biosafety and biosecurity expertise, in line with its statutory mandate. She commended the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, the NCDC, the FCT Health Services Secretariat and their partners for the measures being taken to contain the outbreak. According to her, Nigeria’s experience in containing Ebola in 2014 underscores the importance of preparedness, coordinated action and public cooperation in managing public health emergencies. “Nigeria’s experience in containing Ebola in 2014 demonstrates the importance of preparedness, coordinated action and public cooperation. We must remain vigilant, rely on scientific evidence and adhere to established safety protocols,” she said. The NBMA director-general urged Nigerians to remain calm and vigilant, rely on verified public health information and comply with official advisories. She advised members of the public to practise good hand hygiene, avoid contact with the body fluids of anyone who is ill and refrain from handling the bodies of people suspected to have died from Ebola. Suleiman-Zuntu also cautioned against circulating unverified information capable of creating unnecessary panic, urging Nigerians to support public health authorities by cooperating with contact-tracing efforts. She advised anyone experiencing symptoms consistent with Ebola, particularly after contact with a suspected or confirmed case or travel to an affected area, to promptly seek guidance from public health authorities. The agency urged members of the public seeking verified information, guidance or wishing to report suspected cases to contact the NCDC toll-free line on 6232 or the NBMA on 0808 225 4683. NBMA reiterated its commitment to strengthening biosafety and biosecurity practices and collaborating with relevant national institutions to protect public health and the environment. The post Ebola: NBMA offers experts to support NCDC appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ADC Reps candidate, supporters attacked in Anambra
items.description: By Vincent Ujumadu The African Democratic Congress (ADC) House of Representatives candidate for Idemili North and South Federal Constituency of Anambra State, Hon. Nnamdi Ifebi, and his supporters have reportedly been attacked by suspected thugs during a meeting in Obosi. The assailants, said to be armed with dangerous weapons, reportedly stormed the venue of the meeting and attacked Ifebi and members of the party. They allegedly vandalised the candidate’s campaign vehicle and dispossessed some party members and supporters of personal belongings and empowerment items distributed at the event. The Anambra State Police Public Relations Officer, SP Tochukwu Ikenga, confirmed the incident, adding that the traditional ruler of Obosi, Igwe Chidubem Iweka, who chairs the Anambra State Council of Traditional Rulers, had intervened in the matter. Meanwhile, the state leadership of the ADC has condemned the reported attack, describing it as dangerous and unacceptable ahead of the 2027 general elections. The party’s state Publicity Secretary and Head of Media and Strategic Communications, Comrade Linus Anagboso, said the incident was contrary to democratic principles. He stressed that political competition should be based on ideas, character and service to the people rather than violence and intimidation. “Intimidation, violence or destruction of property should be avoided during this campaign period,” Anagboso said. The ADC called on security agencies to conduct an impartial investigation, identify those responsible and ensure that anyone found culpable faces the full weight of the law. It also urged political stakeholders and supporters across the state to exercise restraint, reject retaliation and respect the right of every citizen to participate freely in the democratic process. “Political differences must never become grounds for violence. Our democracy must be protected and the law must prevail,” Anagboso said. The post ADC Reps candidate, supporters attacked in Anambra appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ¿Sufrió Cataluña el primer ciclón tropical europeo? El Mediterráneo empieza a comportarse como el Caribe
items.description: Los meteorólogos no daban crédito a lo que veían sus ojos: lluvias torrenciales sin una perturbación atmosférica como fuente de inestabilidad que las causara. No había detonante. No había dana . No había vaguada. No había un culpable. Y, sin embargo, visto desde el satélite, en el torbellino de nubes se estaba formando un monstruo: un sistema que se asemejaba a una tormenta tropical en ciernes. Para más pruebas, el radar mostró un viento que podía corresponder a un giro ciclónico cerca de la costa. Si se le hubiera enseñado a un experto en huracanes de EE UU, habría jurado que era un ciclón tropical. El problema es que no estaba gestándose en el mar Caribe, sino en el Mediterráneo, frente a las costas de Cataluña, a 7.000 kilómetros del lugar donde suelen ocurrir. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Bourse de Casablanca : clôture dans le vert
items.description: La Bourse de Casablanca a terminé sur une note positive mercredi, son indice principal, le MASI, gagnant 0,43% à 17.007,86 points (pts). Le MASI 20, qui regroupe les 20 valeurs les plus liquides, a pris 0,79% à 1.233,12 pts, et le MASI ESG, indice des entreprises ayant la meilleure notation ESG selon Moody’s ESG Solutions, a avancé de 0,38% à 1.255,55 pts. Le MASI Mid and Small Cap, reflétant la performance des petites et moyennes entreprises cotées, a augmenté de 0,19% à 1.611,22 pts. Sur le plan sectoriel, les indices « Participation et promotion immobilières » (+2,66%), « Distributeurs » (+2,15%) et « Agroalimentaire / Production » (+1,3%) ont signé les meilleures performances. À l'inverse, les secteurs « Chimie » (-4,68%), « Sylviculture et papier » (-3,07%) et « Sociétés de portefeuilles – Holdings » (-2,18%) ont enregistré les plus fortes baisses. Le volume global des échanges s'est établi à plus de 247,68 millions de dirhams (MDH), dominés par les transactions sur HPS, avec un volume de 58,39 MDH, BCP (54,53 MDH) et Afriquia Gaz (21,73 MDH). La capitalisation boursière a, quant à elle, dépassé 1.000,66 milliards de dirhams. Aux valeurs individuelles, les plus fortes progressions ont été enregistrées par Cosumar (+4,09% à 178 DH), Résidences Dar Saada (+3,16% à 170 DH), Alliances (+2,81% à 366 DH), Label Vie (+2,63% à 3.900 DH) et Stokvis Nord Afrique (+2,4% à 47 DH). À l'opposé, Maghreb Oxygène (-9,38% à 348 DH), Involys (-4,71% à 112,35 DH), SNEP (-3,87% à 273 DH), Med Paper (-3,07% à 22,1 DH) et Cartier Saada (-2,99% à 18,8 DH) ont accusé les plus fortes baisses. items.title: PAC Chair Abena Osei-Asare praises NPA CEO, urges SOEs to address audit findings
items.description: The Chairperson of Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee (PAC), Abena Osei-Asare, has urged state-owned enterprises (SOEs) to take a proactive approach to addressing operational challenges and implementing recommendations arising from audits. She made the call during a visit to the National Petroleum Authority (NPA) on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, where she commended the Authority’s Chief Executive Officer, Godwin Edudzi Tamakloe, for his performance before the Committee. Ms Osei-Asare said she was impressed by Mr Tamakloe’s ability to respond to questions about the Authority’s operations and audit findings. “I must say that I was really impressed with your CEO when he came for the Public Accounts Committee. Where it’s good, I’ll gladly commend you, and when it’s bad too, I won’t mince words,” she said. Ms Osei-Asare said the NPA CEO demonstrated a strong understanding of the issues raised during the Committee’s proceedings. “For every aspect of it, he was able to answer, and I was so impressed also with the audit on the UPPA. I take you to the left, you are able to answer. I bring it to the center, you give me good responses, and to the right, same,” she said. She urged public officials entrusted with managing state institutions to take their responsibilities seriously and protect the resources and assets under their care. “And I think that is what we should all do—that once you are entrusted with something, we should take it seriously and protect it and guard it and pursue it,” she added. She said public officials should perform their duties in a manner that gives confidence to those who appointed them. The PAC Chair stressed that audits should go beyond identifying weaknesses and lead to practical measures to improve institutional systems and procedures. “Audit must lead to certain actions that correct systems, correct procedures, and make things better. That is all the audit is about. It’s not to vilify anybody, but then where we find that we can recover certain things, we recover. Where we need to strengthen systems, we do that. And where obviously there are breaches, sanctions must be carried out,” she said. Ms Osei-Asare explained that the Committee’s visit was intended to give members a better understanding of the NPA’s operations and the processes behind its work. “We just want you to take us through so that when we sit back and we are also asking questions, we know what we are talking about,” she said. The Public Accounts Committee examines public accounts and scrutinises audit findings involving government institutions to promote accountability in the use of public resources. Ms Osei-Asare’s comments reinforce the Committee’s emphasis on ensuring that audit findings lead to recoveries where necessary, stronger internal controls and sanctions where breaches are established. The Committee is continuing its oversight engagements with public institutions, including state-owned enterprises, as part of efforts to improve accountability and the management of public resources.

items.title: CPS pledges deeper collaboration with The Multimedia Group
items.description: The Centre for Policy Scrutiny (CPS), a Ghanaian-based research and policy advocacy think tank, has commended The Multimedia Group for supporting the dissemination of the Centre’s research findings and policy recommendations. A delegation from CPS, led by its Executive Director, Dr Adu Owusu Sarkodie, commended The Multimedia Group for using its platforms to disseminate the think tank’s research and policy review outcomes. He also used the opportunity to call for deeper collaboration between the two institutions as key stakeholders in shaping policy direction and promoting good governance. The Chief Operating Officer of The Multimedia Group, Ken Ansah, commended CPS for its outstanding work, particularly in research and policy advocacy. He urged the think tank to stay focused on its mandate and avoid political influence in carrying out its duties. The two institutions agreed to strengthen their collaboration to promote public education, widen the reach of policy research and encourage informed discussions on national development issues. CPS conducts research and policy analysis to scrutinise public policies, assess government programmes, and recommend improvements to governance and development outcomes. Its publications include Improved Access, Quality Questioned: A Report on 9 Years of Ghana’s Free Senior High School Policy, which examines the implementation and outcomes of the Free SHS programme. The Centre has also analysed Ghana’s 2026 Budget and Mid-Year Budget Review, focusing on public finance and economic management. The CPS Executive Director was accompanied by the Head of Corporate Affairs, Kwaku Obeng-Adjei, and the Programmes Officer, Nana Yaa Dapaah.

items.title: Kano police recover ₦8m stolen car, arrest mechanic
items.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The Kano State Police Command has recovered a Kia Optima valued at ₦8 million and arrested a 24-year-old mechanic, Mubarak Muktar, in connection with the stolen vehicle. The black 2014-model car was reportedly stolen on October 4, 2026, after the owner’s wife parked it in front of Ziha Health Care in Karkasara Quarters, Tarauni Local Government Area of Kano State. The owner, a resident of Sharada Phase II, reportedly reported the theft to the police at about 7:20 p.m. on the same day. In a statement issued on Wednesday, the command’s Public Relations Officer, CSP Abdullahi Haruna Kiyawa, said operatives of the Special Intervention Squad launched an investigation following the report. “On October 18, at about 5 p.m., operatives of the Special Intervention Squad arrested Mubarak Muktar at Farm Centre Garage in Tarauni, where he was found in possession of the stolen vehicle. “Preliminary investigation revealed that the suspect was the mechanic responsible for the vehicle and was found in possession of it at his garage,” the statement said. The police said investigations were ongoing to establish further details surrounding the incident. According to the statement, the recovered vehicle was handed over to its owner after the police verified ownership. The owner reportedly expressed appreciation to the police for recovering the car. The Commissioner of Police, Ibrahim Adamu Bakori, commended the officers involved in the operation, describing the recovery as part of the command’s efforts to tackle property-related crimes under Operation Kukan Kura. Bakori also advised vehicle owners to exercise caution when selecting mechanics and ensure they entrust their vehicles to trusted and verified professionals. The post Kano police recover ₦8m stolen car, arrest mechanic appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Manga : La 2e édition du festival des terres du Nazinon célèbre la culture et la cohésion sociale
items.description: La 2ᵉ édition du Festival des Terres du Nazinon a été officiellement lancée le mardi 20 octobre 2026 à Manga, dans la région du Nazinon. Placée sous le thème « Unité, culture, paix et jeunesse », cette édition a été présidée par le ministre de l’Éducation nationale, de l’Alphabétisation et de la Promotion des langues nationales, Sosthène Dingara, en présence de la ministre de la Transition digitale, des Postes et des Communications électroniques, Aminata Zerbo/Sabané. Pendant une semaine, la « belle cité de l’Épervier » célébrera la culture dans la région du Nazinon, dans un esprit de fraternité et d’unité, à l’occasion de la 2ᵉ édition du Festival des Terres du Nazinon. Les officiels présents Selon la promotrice du festival, Denise Koudougou/Oulon, cet événement est né d’une volonté de promouvoir la culture et de valoriser le patrimoine national. « un peuple qui connaît ses racines, protège son patrimoine et valorise ses traditions se donne les moyens de bâtir durablement son avenir. C’est cette conviction qui a présidé à la création du Festival des Terres du Nazinon en 2025 », a-t-elle déclaré. Pour Denise Koudougou/Oulon, le thème retenu pour cette édition n’est pas anodin. Il met en avant des valeurs essentielles telles que la paix, l’unité et la cohésion sociale, dans un contexte où la culture peut contribuer au rapprochement des populations. Denise Koudougou/Oulon explique son attachement à la culture La promotrice a également expliqué que le festival vise à faire connaître les savoir-faire de la région et du Burkina Faso, aussi bien auprès des populations locales que des visiteurs venus d’ailleurs. L’ambition est de susciter l’intérêt pour les richesses culturelles du pays et d’encourager leur appropriation. Prenant la parole, le ministre de l’Éducation nationale, de l’Alphabétisation et de la Promotion des langues nationales, Sosthène Dingara, a rappelé l’importance du patrimoine culturel dans la construction du Burkina Faso. Il a notamment souligné que les traditions, les savoir-faire, la créativité et les expressions artistiques constituent des ressources stratégiques pour le développement endogène. Le ministre Dingara exprime sa satisfaction Le programme de cette deuxième édition prévoit des prestations artistiques, des expositions, des animations ainsi que des rencontres autour du patrimoine culturel. Les festivaliers sont également invités à découvrir les produits locaux et les expressions culturelles qui contribuent à l’identité du Nazinon. À travers cette deuxième édition, le Festival des Terres du Nazinon entend ainsi renforcer sa place dans le paysage culturel burkinabè et faire de la culture un levier de promotion de la paix, de l’unité et du développement local. items.title: Websites go dark worldwide as AI exposes critical security flaws
items.description: Government agencies and companies around the world shut down websites Wednesday after two critical flaws came to light involving PHP, a programming language that is the basis for a large share of the internet. The US National Security Agency told organizations to patch immediately or pull vulnerable systems offline. The flaws “often provide a direct path to the server’s file system or database,” the NSA said in a statement on X. Attackers could use them to take over web servers without needing a password. PHP sits underneath popular web design platforms so the weaknesses potentially affect a vast range of websites, from online stores and news outlets to government services. The discovery came amid a surge in software security disclosures driven by increasingly powerful AI models, with the number of vulnerabilities found in 2026 on track to roughly double last year’s record total. PHP volunteers released a fix on Wednesday. “If you run PHP, it is imperative that you update now,” the PHP Foundation, which funds developers working on the language, said in a blog post. The flaws were reported in August by security firm Calif and by ChatGPT maker OpenAI, which flagged them independently on the same day. Google-owned cloud security company Wiz later reported further ways to exploit them. The flaws had been reported privately to PHP’s developers at the time and kept confidential while a fix was prepared. Details leaked online Tuesday, a day before the planned release, prompting the rush to take sites offline. In France, local government websites, including the Paris Police Prefecture, have been inaccessible since Wednesday afternoon at the request of the French National Cybersecurity Agency, following “detection of a critical security vulnerability,” the Ministry of the Interior said. In the Netherlands, the national digital identity service DigiD, the website of the House of Representatives and the site of the national cybersecurity center went offline as a precaution, according to Dutch public broadcaster NOS. Belgium’s foreign ministry temporarily took its websites offline as a precaution, it said on X, although the Centre for Cybersecurity Belgium had recorded no attacks on Belgian sites. AFP The post Websites go dark worldwide as AI exposes critical security flaws appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Mine Murder Trial: Court grants bail to four defendants
items.description: Ogbegbe remains in custody as court adjourns for final addresses By Egufe Yafugborhi ASABA — The Delta State High Court in Asaba on Wednesday granted bail to four defendants standing trial over the fatal shooting of Oghenemi “Mine” Ogidi in Effurun, Delta State, while the first defendant, ASP Usman Nuhu, popularly known as “Ogbegbe”, remains in prison custody. The development followed the closure of the defence cases by all five defendants in the trial over the April 26 incident. The trial judge, Justice Michael Obi, granted bail to the second to fifth defendants — Onoloko Dauroupamo, Okoh Kelechi, Goodluck Kingsley and Omonigho Ahweyevu. The defendants were members of the Anti-Crime Squad led by Nuhu at the Effurun Area Command of the Nigeria Police Force before they were dismissed by the police authorities following the incident. Speaking to journalists after Wednesday’s proceedings, counsel to Nuhu, Uche Chibuogwu, said he did not consider it necessary to apply for bail for his client, citing concerns for his safety and the gravity of the murder charge. “Today, we opened our defence for the first defendant, and we concluded our case. The second, third, fourth and fifth defendants’ counsel did the same, too. The second to the fifth defendants were granted bail because bail applications were filed on their behalf,” he said. Why We Didn’t Seek Bail for Nuhu — Counsel Chibuogwu explained that he deliberately refrained from filing a bail application for Nuhu. “We did not find it necessary filing bail application for the first defendant, one, for his own safety, and secondly, this is a capital offence — offence of murder,” he said. He acknowledged the loss suffered by the deceased’s family and friends, describing the case as a difficult one to handle as defence counsel. “Like I said on the 6th of October, the victim, the deceased person, has family, has friends. So, justice is for the deceased, for the society, and for other defendants. Justice should be for all. And this court is a court of equity,” he said. He added that although the case was difficult, he had a constitutional duty to represent his client. “For the deceased person, like I said earlier, it’s quite unfortunate. And this defence is a difficult one for me, but I have to do my constitutional duty as a lawyer,” he said. On the bail conditions imposed on the four defendants, Chibuogwu said their sureties must reside within the court’s jurisdiction, provide evidence of tax payment for three years and valid tax clearance certificates, and deposit their National Identification Number cards with the court. He said the parties would return to court on November 17 to adopt their final written addresses, after which the court would proceed towards judgment. Prosecution Explains Bail Decision The Delta State Director of Public Prosecutions, Tejiri R. Anuwhin, who led the prosecution, also confirmed that all five defendants had opened and closed their defence cases. Anuwhin said the prosecution had earlier closed its case after calling six witnesses, adding that the defendants subsequently gave evidence and called a witness during their defence. “So today, the last time we came to court, we (prosecution) closed our case after feeding six witnesses. Today was the turn of the defence to open their case, and the defendants — five of them — opened their defence, gave evidence, and also called a witness they have. “They also closed their case, and now we’ve adjourned the case to the 17th of November for adoption of final written addresses,” he said. Explaining why the court granted bail to the second to fifth defendants, the DPP said the offences they faced, which bordered on negligence, carried a maximum prison term of six months. He noted that the four defendants had been in custody since June 1, adding that the court considered the period they had already spent in detention in reaching its decision. “So ordinarily, if they were found guilty, they would have almost served that term of imprisonment,” he said. Anuwhin said the court granted bail on the condition that the defendants produced suitable sureties who would ensure their attendance at subsequent proceedings. According to him, each surety was required to provide a N2 million undertaking, possess a National Identification Number and reside within the court’s jurisdiction. He said the parties would adopt their final written addresses at the next hearing, after which the court would adjourn the matter for judgment. Odogwu Asaaba Faces Rape, Manslaughter Charges Meanwhile, in a separate case before Justice Obi, content creator Ifeanyi Ogbonna, popularly known as Odogwu Asaaba, pleaded not guilty to a two-count charge of rape and manslaughter over the death of Favour Agbro. Delta State Solicitor-General, Omamuzo Erebe, SAN, appeared for the state. Justice Obi adjourned the case until October 28 for the commencement of trial. items.title: Muere un trabajador forestal por un ataque masivo de avispas velutinas en Ourense
items.description: Un hombre de más de 50 años estaba realizando trabajos de desbroce en una pista forestal del municipio ourensano de Larouco cuando se topó, este miércoles al mediodía, con un nido de avispas velutinas . Los insectos lo atacaron masivamente y falleció casi en el acto, sin que los servicios de emergencias llegasen a tiempo para suministrarle el antídoto y salvar su vida. Al lugar de los hechos se desplazaron una ambulancia medicalizada y un helicóptero, además del médico del ayuntamiento de Larouco y un equipo de emergencias . La víctima, José E.A., natural del municipio pontevedrés de O Porriño, al sur de Vigo, llevaba muchos años residiendo en el ayuntamiento ourensano de Manzaneda. Actualmente trabajaba como alumno en un taller de empleo que daba servicio a varios consistorios de la zona: Larouco, Manzaneda, O Bolo y San Xoán de Río, en Ourense. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Des agents réquisitionnés pour assurer la continuité du service public
items.description: La Direction générale de la société de transport public Dakar Dem Dikk annonce la réquisition de certains agents pour la période du 21 au 23 octobre 2026. Une mesure destinée à maintenir les dessertes prioritaires et à garantir la sécurité des usagers. La continuité du service public de transport est au cœur d’une nouvelle mesure prise par la société Dakar Dem Dikk. Dans un communiqué daté du 21 octobre 2026, la Direction générale informe de la réquisition de certains agents pour une durée de trois jours, du 21 au 23 octobre inclus. Cette décision intervient en application de l’arrêté n° 0199/GRD/AD du gouverneur de la région de Dakar, en date du 21 octobre 2026. Selon le communiqué, « les agents désignés sont réquisitionnés pour la période du 21 au 23 octobre 2026 inclus ». Lire aussi: Des agents réquisitionnés du 21 au 23 octobre Les agents concernés sont tenus de rejoindre leur poste conformément aux affectations et aux horaires prévus. La Direction générale leur demande de se mettre « sans délai à la disposition de leurs responsables » afin d’assurer les missions qui leur sont confiées. Le dispositif prévoit également un suivi de l’exécution de cette mesure. Les responsables de service sont ainsi chargés de veiller à la présence effective du personnel réquisitionné et à la bonne exécution des missions assignées. À travers cette décision, Dakar Dem Dikk entend préserver le fonctionnement du service public de transport durant la période concernée. La Direction générale précise qu’elle veillera à la stricte application de la mesure, dont les objectifs sont d’assurer « la continuité du service public de transport, le maintien des dessertes prioritaires et la sécurité des usagers ». items.title: Gender Ministry supports 625 flood-affected residents in Hohoe with emergency cash
items.description: The Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection (MoGCSP) has provided emergency cash assistance to 625 people affected by flooding in Hohoe in the Volta Region to help them meet their immediate needs and recover from the disaster. The intervention, delivered through the Livelihood Empowerment Against Poverty (LEAP) Programme, follows flooding that struck parts of the municipality on September 28, 2026. The floods, triggered by heavy rainfall and the overflow of the River Dayi, damaged homes and properties, disrupted livelihoods and left several families in need of urgent assistance. During a visit to the affected communities on September 30, the Minister for Gender, Children and Social Protection, Dr Agnes Naa Momo Lartey, interacted with residents and assessed the extent of the damage. Following the visit, the Minister directed that measures be put in place to assist affected households, ease their hardship and support their recovery. The emergency cash assistance is intended to help beneficiaries purchase food and essential household items, replace lost belongings and cover other urgent expenses resulting from the flooding. The Ministry expects the intervention to provide financial relief to affected families as they work to restore their livelihoods and rebuild their lives. The 625 beneficiaries constitute the first batch of identified flood-affected households receiving assistance under the intervention.

items.title: Reps urge FG to resolve BEDC dispute, restore power
items.description: By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has urged the Federal Government to intervene in the dispute between the National Union of Electricity Employees (NUEE) and the Benin Electricity Distribution Company (BEDC) to restore electricity supply to Edo, Delta, Ondo and Ekiti states. The House warned that the prolonged disruption could endanger lives, cripple essential services and worsen the economic challenges facing residents and businesses in the affected states. The resolution followed the adoption of a motion of urgent national importance sponsored by Clement Jimbo, a member of the House from Akwa Ibom State. Presenting the motion, Jimbo expressed concern that the dispute had disrupted electricity supply and forced some critical services to shut down, warning that a prolonged blackout could undermine healthcare delivery, water supply, telecommunications, banking and educational activities. “The disruption of electricity supply over 24 hours, if sustained, poses a serious threat to public safety, socio-economic activities and the delivery of essential services across the affected states,” he said. Jimbo warned that the outage could also disrupt medical services in hospitals, laboratories, maternity centres and emergency units, particularly facilities dependent on electricity to operate life-support equipment and preserve temperature-sensitive medical supplies. He added that small businesses and public infrastructure reliant on regular electricity supply would suffer significant setbacks if the situation persisted. The lawmaker also expressed concern that alternative energy sources, including solar power, might provide limited relief during the rainy season because of reduced sunlight for charging batteries. Following the adoption of the motion by a majority of lawmakers at plenary, the House called on the Federal Government, through relevant electricity-sector authorities, to intervene and facilitate an amicable and lasting resolution between NUEE and BEDC. The House also mandated its Committees on Power and Labour and Employment to investigate the circumstances surrounding the dispute, identify the immediate causes of the disruption and recommend measures to prevent a recurrence. It urged the union and BEDC management to resume dialogue and negotiations, stressing the need for both parties to take urgent steps to restore electricity supply to affected communities. The lawmakers further called on relevant authorities to make alternative electricity arrangements for hospitals, emergency medical facilities and other critical public services pending the restoration of normal supply. The House said resolving the dispute was necessary to protect public safety, sustain economic activities and prevent further disruption to essential services across the four states. It stressed the need for a lasting solution that would address the underlying disagreements between the workers’ union and the distribution company while ensuring reliable electricity supply to affected communities. items.title: Ebola: Reps urge calm, compliance with health guidelines
items.description: By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja The House of Representatives Committee on Infectious Diseases has urged Nigerians to remain calm and comply with preventive health guidelines amid concerns over a possible Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) threat. The committee also called on the Federal Government to strengthen disease surveillance, screening, contact tracing and emergency response measures to prevent a potential outbreak. The committee’s chairman, Amobi Godwin Ogah, made the call on Wednesday in Abuja while leading members of the committee at a briefing with journalists. Ogah stressed the importance of public vigilance, early detection and strict adherence to official health advisories, warning that delays in identifying suspected cases and tracing contacts could increase the risk of transmission. The appeal followed reports of a confirmed Ebola case involving a woman who reportedly arrived in Abuja from Uganda on October 20, 2026, with health authorities said to be tracing 44 contacts for isolation and further testing. The lawmakers urged Nigerians to rely on verified information from the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare and the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), rather than unverified reports capable of triggering unnecessary panic. They also called on federal and state health agencies to intensify surveillance, strengthen screening at points of entry, expand laboratory testing, and ensure effective contact tracing and emergency response. The committee identified public awareness, adequate infection prevention and control supplies, healthcare workers’ preparedness and sufficient funding as critical measures for containing any potential outbreak. It urged the Federal Government to mobilise public and private health institutions to strengthen preparedness and response efforts, while calling for the immediate release of outstanding appropriated funds to relevant health agencies. The lawmakers further asked the Ministry of Health and Social Welfare and the NCDC to assess the country’s preparedness and response capacity in line with current epidemiological evidence and public health guidance. The committee pledged to engage relevant ministries, departments and agencies, as well as public health institutions, to obtain updates on the situation and report its findings to the House for possible legislative action. It also underscored the need for collaboration with the World Health Organisation (WHO) and other regional and international public health institutions to ensure that Nigeria’s response is guided by scientific evidence and international health regulations. Ebola Virus Disease is a severe infectious disease that can be fatal. Prompt detection, appropriate medical care and coordinated public health interventions are essential to limiting its spread. The lawmakers maintained that timely intervention by health authorities, alongside public cooperation and compliance with official guidelines, would be critical to protecting lives and safeguarding public health. items.title: Seven missing fishermen make contact after a week adrift at sea
items.description: Seven fishermen missing at sea for more than a week have reportedly made contact by phone, saying their canoe, Second Chance, is stranded far offshore after an engine failure. One of the crew members, Kwame Akyim, told TV3 News reporter Abraham Mensah in a telephone interview that the canoe’s outboard motor had failed, leaving the seven men drifting in open waters. According to Mr Akyim, strong tides carried the canoe more than 120 nautical miles offshore. “We had an engine failure with the outboard motor,” he said. He said the crew later used canvas to help move the canoe but remained stranded, with limited food and no assistance. “We haven’t had a decent meal for over a week. We had to feed on the fish we had caught. We have been praying since,” Mr Akyim said. The crew member also claimed that they had resorted to boiling seawater for drinking. “We boil seawater and drink it,” he said. Despite the reported hardship, Mr Akyim said the seven men were generally in stable condition, although one crew member had experienced stomach pain. He expressed frustration over what he described as unsuccessful attempts to attract the attention of passing vessels. “No one is responding to our call,” he said. “Ships move past us and do not heed our distress call,” he added. The Western Regional Marine Police Command had earlier announced a coordinated search for the canoe and its seven crew members. The canoe’s owner, Nana Kweku Atta, reported its disappearance to the Fishing Harbour Police Station in Sekondi on October 18 after it failed to return from a fishing expedition off Axim. The canoe departed Sekondi Fishing Harbour on October 9. Preliminary information from the police suggested that the canoe may have suffered engine failure and drifted towards Tema and the Volta coast. Its last known position had not been confirmed. The Ghana Navy, Ghana Maritime Authority, Fisheries Commission, relevant coastal police stations and fishing communities had been alerted to assist in the search. The latest account from the crew may provide a critical lead for rescue teams, although their current location and the status of rescue efforts remain to be confirmed. The seven fishermen are Kwame Akyim, 42; Uncle Amoah, 27; Kobina Koom, 38; Emma, 39; Oboy, 28; Kwamena, 40; and Abodwe, 38.

items.title: Aguocha denies selling rice donated to Abia constituents
items.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — The member representing Ikwuano/Umuahia Federal Constituency of Abia State in the House of Representatives, Hon. Obi Aguocha, has denied allegations that he diverted and sold two truckloads of rice donated to his constituents by President Bola Tinubu. A former Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs in Abia State, Chief Charles Ogbonna, had accused the lawmaker of diverting the rice and selling it in the market in connivance with his in-law. Ogbonna challenged Aguocha to sue him if the allegations were untrue. However, in a statement, Aguocha described the allegations as false, malicious and fabricated, insisting that neither he nor anyone acting under his direction diverted, converted or sold any truckload of rice or palliatives. He said all food relief items allocated to his constituents under the relevant appropriation provisions were distributed transparently and directly to the people through established and verifiable community-based channels. Describing the allegations as a smear campaign against him, Aguocha said his relationship with Ogbonna deteriorated after he cautioned the former commissioner against making what he described as unfounded allegations against Abia State Governor, Alex Otti. The lawmaker, who is seeking re-election in 2027, alleged that his political opponents had resorted to spreading false claims because they could not defeat him in a fair election. He accused them of attempting to damage his reputation and diminish his political standing ahead of the polls. “Beyond the obvious attempt at character assassination, this orchestrated campaign was deliberate in its design to incite my constituents to anger, hatred, and mob violence against my person and office. “In a challenging economic climate, falsely telling citizens that public palliatives meant for them were stolen and sold is a dangerous, reckless tactic calculated to trigger civil unrest and bodily harm,” he said. Aguocha vowed to institute legal action against Ogbonna and others allegedly involved in the accusations, adding that his legal team was already compiling evidence. He urged his constituents to remain calm and vigilant, insisting that the allegations would not distract him from his re-election bid in 2027. The post Aguocha denies selling rice donated to Abia constituents appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: COMMUNIQUÉ DE PRESSE: TRANSLOG AFRICA 2026 : SITARAIL, ABIDJAN TERMINAL, CÔTE D’IVOIRE TERMINAL ET AGL BF, AU RENDEZ-VOUS DE LA LOGISTIQUE AFRICAINE
items.description: Depuis le 20 octobre et jusqu’au 22 octobre 2026, Ouagadougou accueille la 5ᵉ édition de TRANSLOG Africa, organisée par le Conseil Burkinabè des Chargeurs (CBC) autour du thème : « Résilience et sécurisation des chaînes logistiques dans un environnement mondial en pleine mutation ». À cette occasion, SITARAIL, ABIDJAN TERMINAL, CÔTE D’IVOIRE TERMINAL et AGL BF, quatre filiales du groupe Africa Global Logistics (AGL), sont au rendez-vous. Leur participation illustre la complémentarité des solutions ferroviaires, portuaires et logistiques pour améliorer la fluidité des échanges, renforcer la compétitivité des corridors régionaux et sécuriser les chaînes d’approvisionnement, notamment vers les pays de l’hinterland. C'est dans cette dynamique que SITARAIL, opérant le chemin de fer et maillon incontournable de la chaîne logistique entre la Côte d’Ivoire et le Burkina Faso, a assuré une communication développée par sa directrice commerciale Nadège DIARRA autour du thème : « Performance des corridors de transit vers les pays enclavés : enjeux des coûts, contraintes, gouvernance et coordination des acteurs. » À travers cette participation active, les quatre entreprises contribuent aux réflexions sur l’avenir de la logistique africaine, en misant sur la complémentarité de leurs expertises, la modernisation des équipements et une meilleure coordination des acteurs. « L'appartenance à la famille MSC nous permet d'offrir une solution intégrée de bout en bout d'une fluidité remarquable. Dès l'arrivée du navire au Port d'Abidjan, la synergie s'opère : Abidjan Terminal et Côte d'Ivoire Terminal assurent des opérations de manutention de classe mondiale avec des cadences de débarquement optimales. SITARAIL prend ensuite le relais direct sur le rail pour le pré/post- acheminement terrestre vers le Burkina Faso. Enfin, AGL (Africa Global Logistics) orchestre les prestations logistiques, de transit et de stockage dans l'hinterland. Cette complémentarité élimine les ruptures de charge et garantit un service continu, rapide et sécurisé pour l'ensemble des opérateurs économiques » a souligné Nadège DIARRA . À propos de SITARAIL SITARAIL, filiale d’Africa Global Logistics (AGL), exploite le réseau ferroviaire entre la Côte d’Ivoire et le Burkina Faso depuis août 1995 dans le cadre d’un partenariat public-privé (PPP). L’entreprise transporte en moyenne un million de tonnes de fret chaque année. Avant la pandémie de COVID-19, elle assurait également le transport annuel de plus de 200 000 voyageurs. SITARAIL emploie environ 1 500 collaborateurs et constitue, grâce à ses activités et à ses actions en faveur de la santé, de l’éducation et de l’environnement, un acteur essentiel du développement socio-économique et de l’intégration régionale en Afrique de l’Ouest. A ce jour, SITARAIL investit dans la modernisation de ses équipements de maintenance, de ses systèmes d’exploitation et dans le renforcement de son parc roulant. Elle reste également mobilisée pour accompagner les projets de renaissance du réseau Abidjan-Ouagadougou-Kaya, à travers notamment le Plan d’urgence et le Programme de réhabilitation intégrale portés par les États de Côte d’Ivoire et du Burkina. Contact Presse : Mathieu SOUBEIGA, Chef Département Communication et Relations extérieures – SITARAIL mathieu.soubeiga@sitarail.com – Tel : +226 56 94 53 93 / +225 07 999 751 29 Sensitivity: Internal The post COMMUNIQUÉ DE PRESSE: TRANSLOG AFRICA 2026 : SITARAIL, ABIDJAN TERMINAL, CÔTE D’IVOIRE TERMINAL ET AGL BF, AU RENDEZ-VOUS DE LA LOGISTIQUE AFRICAINE appeared first on L'economiste du faso .

items.title: The Texas Race Worth Watching
items.description: A crucial midterm contest is happening right now in Texas, one that could determine the future of the state and its influence on federal policy and national politics. No, not the U.S. Senate race—though everyone is watching that one, and with good reason. The Republican, Ken Paxton—who has served as Texas’s attorney general since 2015—is an unusually weak candidate, beset by personal and financial scandals and a reputation for using his office for right-wing culture-war fixations, and weighed down by a deeply unpopular president. On the other side is James Talarico, an unusually strong Democratic candidate, fluent in the language of faith and without the cloud of scandal that haunts his opponent. “This is the most competitive election that we have seen in Texas” in decades, James Henson, the executive director of the University of Texas at Austin’s nonpartisan Texas Politics Project , told me. But the race I’m talking about is downstream of that: Who will succeed Ken Paxton? The two major-party candidates vying to be attorney general are Nathan Johnson, a Democratic state senator from Dallas, and Mayes Middleton (“MAGA Mayes,” as his own ads call him), a Republican state senator and GOP mega-donor whose district covers parts of Harris, Brazoria, and Galveston counties. An October poll from the Texas Politics Project shows a dead heat, with Johnson at 48 percent and Middleton at 47 percent. The Texas attorney general is a very powerful position, one that has frequently been a springboard to higher office—John Cornyn held the job before becoming a U.S. senator, as did Greg Abbott before becoming the state’s governor. The AG is meant to defend the laws of the state, and has certain specific responsibilities, such as enforcing child support and investigating Medicaid fraud. Over the past few decades, however, the role has become something more: a way for ambitious politicians to wage culture wars, cultivate a national profile by taking on right-wing causes, and shape law and policy not just in Texas but nationwide. The attorney general “helps set legal policy across the country,” Justin Nelson, a Democrat who came within a few points of unseating Paxton in 2018, told me. The race between Talarico and Paxton may be capturing everyone’s attention right now, but “when you’re a senator, you’re one of 100,” Nelson pointed out. There’s only one attorney general of Texas. When Abbott was Texas attorney general under the Obama administration, he used to joke , “I go into the office, I sue the federal government and I go home.” Paxton—who was acquitted by the Senate in a 2023 trial over accusations of corruption and bribery—has been even more pugnacious. Early in his tenure as attorney general, Paxton encouraged clerks to refuse to issue marriage licenses to same-sex couples. He used the office to sue the developers of a mosque and housing community north of Dallas for securities fraud ; the case fueled right-wing conspiracy theories nationwide about the “Islamization of Texas.” (A state securities commissioner described the case as “horseshit”—ironically, Paxton himself was accused of securities fraud .) He wrote a memo that designated puberty blockers and other gender-affirming health care “child abuse” and that kicked off Child Protective Services investigations of parents of trans children , and most recently used the state’s consumer-protection law to target pediatricians who vaccinate children. He has threatened to investigate public schools to ensure they’re displaying the Ten Commandments. He also filed the case asking the Supreme Court to overturn the results of the 2020 election. He has tried to prevent women whose pregnancies meet the state’s extremely narrow standards for legal abortion from accessing the procedure. After a court order gave one woman whose child had a fatal abnormality permission to get an abortion, Paxton threatened any doctor who dared perform it, warning that the judge’s order “will not insulate hospitals, doctors, or anyone else, from civil and criminal liability.” Paxton has also tried to sue doctors in other states for allegedly providing abortion medication to Texas residents—an issue that is almost certain to end up at the Supreme Court sooner or later, much like Texas’s original abortion bounty law did , in a foreshadowing of the 2022 Dobbs decision overturning Roe v. Wade . These cases and others have shaped abortion policy nationally , not just in Texas. [ Read: Ken Paxton is actually doing this ] An entire accounting of Paxton’s use of the AG’s office to further extreme conservative causes would take too long. But you get the idea. The Texas AG’s office is the “largest legal power in the conservative movement, nationally, period, end of story,” Adam Piper, who runs the Republican Attorneys General Association, told The Texas Tribune earlier this year. Ali S. Zaidi, the former director of the Texas House Democratic Caucus, told me that “simply removing a Republican” from the Texas attorney general’s office “could have enormous ripple effects across the country for, frankly, generations to come.” Paxton’s aggressive use of the office isn’t an exclusively right-wing phenomenon; Democratic AGs from California, New York, and other states have been at the forefront of litigation against President Trump’s tariffs, his environmental policies, and his attempt to repeal birthright citizenship. AGs have also pursued consumer-protection issues that the federal government mostly abandoned. But Nathan Johnson is not presenting himself as that kind of candidate. Instead, he says he wants to return the office to what he sees as its traditional role: “It is there to protect consumers from predatory business practices; it is there to investigate shady relationships between the private sector and the public sector; it is there to keep the system of checks and balances in place in government.” This is surely a smart pitch for such a red state, and the race is quite close for a place where Democrats haven’t won statewide office since Pulp Fiction was in theaters. Nevertheless, Texas Republicans’ objections to Paxton are less about policy and more about ethics. “I think Mayes Middleton is a stronger candidate than Ken Paxton,” Nelson said, describing Paxton as perhaps the “most corrupt public official in the country.” Matt Mackowiak, a Republican political consultant, told me that Middleton’s policy views “align with a majority of Texans.” This state has been red for three decades. Voters may be tired of Paxton’s baggage, but that doesn’t mean they’re tired of having a state attorney general who tries to move the state and the country in a conservative direction. W hoever becomes the next attorney general, he’ll be tasked with enforcing Texas law, which includes that near ban on abortion and a series of restrictions on trans rights that frightened some families so much that they ultimately fled the state . But there’s a difference between enforcing the law and what Paxton has done, which is interpret the law so aggressively that, for example, a pregnant woman whose fetus has a fatal abnormality has to leave the state just to get care. Johnson told me that Paxton’s attempt to sue doctors in New York, Delaware, and California over abortion medication that is banned in Texas was “legally ridiculous.” Texas law, he said, does not apply outside of Texas. Johnson said he is “not opposed to immigration enforcement” but that he would sue the federal government if immigration authorities violate Texas residents’ constitutional rights. He called the law passed last year requiring public schools to display the Ten Commandments unconstitutional, and said he would not strong-arm any schools who declined to follow the law “until the Supreme Court says otherwise.” He also decried Paxton’s effort to use driver’s-license data from the Department of Public Safety to create a registry of transgender Texans. Johnson’s approach, he suggested, would be to simply leave trans people alone. “We’re talking about not abusing your power to make certain people miserable, to rally your base,” he said. “And I’m happy to say that I don’t think that kind of behavior is being rewarded politically right now in Texas.” [ Carlos Sanchez: How Texas’s attorney general won by losing big ] Still, Texas has arguably gotten redder in the past six years. Trump beat Hillary Clinton in the state in 2016 by nine points, Biden by about six, and Harris by about 14. Even in a midterm year with an unpopular incumbent president weighing down the GOP ticket, Democrats have a lot to overcome. Middleton also has a lot more money. In the candidates’ most recent campaign-finance reports, Johnson had taken in a little more than $1 million, whereas Middleton—the inheritor of his father’s oil-and-gas company—had almost $3.5 million in contributions. That money could make a big difference, especially since neither candidate has much name recognition. In the Texas Politics Project poll, 40 percent of voters had no opinion of Middleton, and 48 percent had no opinion of Johnson. But Zaidi told me that Johnson, being part of the class-of-2018 Democrats who entered office during Trump’s first term, was well equipped to compete in Texas. These officials know how to take on big “policy fights, but in a way that’s not a turnoff for the median voter,” Zaidi said, pointing to Johnson’s work trying to expand Medicaid in Texas —a popular policy but one that Republican state lawmakers have blocked. The AG race—and those of other state offices—may be decided by the top of the ticket. Johnson, Nelson said, will “rise or fall depending on how well” Talarico and the Democratic candidate for governor, Gina Hinojosa, do. “I think Nathan is well positioned to ride a wave. He’s got his surfboard out.” If Middleton triumphs, he seems intent on continuing Abbott’s and Cornyn’s legacies. Middleton has said that “there’s no such thing as separation of church and state,” and that “one of the most important things here is backing up President Trump and his border security and deportation agenda.” A recent campaign ad boasts of Middleton’s support of the state’s bathroom bill , “Mayes Middleton: kicking perverted men out of women’s restrooms and locker rooms.” This seems to be a subject of particular importance to Middleton, who recently told an audience that Johnson will “fight to get men in your little girl’s restroom and locker room.” Nelson believes that, after 30 years of Republican control, Texans are getting tired of these culture wars. They hear Republicans talking about trans people in bathrooms, and they’re “like, Yeah, cool, man, but why is cereal eight bucks and I don’t know if my kid’s gonna have a job? ” The GOP thinks Texans are looking for an ethical conservative who will pursue the same causes as Paxton, and the Dems are betting on widespread fatigue not just with Paxton personally, but with conservative culture-war politics. These visions may be miles apart politically, but as far as the polls are concerned, for now, they’re neck and neck.

items.title: Our political differences will not diminish my affection for Kwankwaso — Tinubu
items.description: President Bola Tinubu has congratulated former Kano State Governor, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, on his 70th birthday, saying their political differences will not diminish his affection for the former Minister of Defence. Tinubu, in a congratulatory message issued on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, described Kwankwaso as a longtime friend and political associate whose contributions to Nigeria’s democratic development remain significant. The President recalled that their relationship dated back to 1992, when both served in the National Assembly, with Kwankwaso in the House of Representatives and Tinubu in the Senate. He said their political association continued in 1999 when they both emerged as governors of their respective states. “As members of the Class of ’99 Governors, we both played pivotal roles in laying the foundation for the democracy the nation enjoys today,” Tinubu said. According to him, their political paths later diverged because of different political choices before they came together in 2013 to form the All Progressives Congress. “Since then, history and service have kept us intertwined,” he added. Tinubu acknowledged Kwankwaso’s contributions to Kano State and Nigeria, citing his service as a two-term governor, Minister of Defence, senator representing Kano Central Senatorial District and presidential candidate. He also noted Kwankwaso’s current role as a presidential running mate, describing him as an influential figure and progressive politician. The President said their membership of different political parties and participation on competing platforms in the January 2027 election would not affect his personal regard for the former Kano governor. “That we are in different political parties and competing on different platforms in the January 2027 election will not remove my affection for Senator Kwankwaso,” he said. Tinubu wished Kwankwaso good health, personal fulfilment and many more years of active participation in Nigeria’s democratic process as he marked the milestone. items.title: He’s a Northern kid — Sowunmi slams Baba-Ahmed for calling Tinubu ‘a failure’
items.description: By Bayo Wahab Segun Sowunmi, a chieftain of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and member of the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council, has described Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, chairman of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), as a “Northern kid” following his criticism of President Bola Tinubu’s administration. Baba-Ahmed had described Tinubu as a failure, arguing that although the president inherited a poor country with weak institutions, poverty and insecurity, he had spent three and a half years in office without delivering the expected results. But Sowunmi, who spoke on Vanguard’s Politics Hub on Wednesday, faulted the PRP chairman’s assessment, questioning his criticism of the president and challenging Northern leaders to reflect on the region’s development. “That’s a Northern kid. What did I say? He’s a Northern kid. When you behave like a kid, you are a kid,” Sowunmi said. The PDP chieftain, who said he grew up and attended school in Kaduna, said he remained concerned about the North and its development. He questioned the outcomes of resources allocated to the region over the years, arguing that its leaders should examine their own responsibilities rather than focus solely on criticising the president. “All the resources that have been allocated to the North, where is the result?” he asked. Sowunmi also invoked the legacies of Nigeria’s former leaders from the region, including Tafawa Balewa and Ahmadu Bello, questioning whether they would be satisfied with the North’s present condition. He said leaders should be willing to confront the region’s challenges honestly instead of becoming “so loudmouthed” when criticising people from outside it. Describing Baba-Ahmed as a “rabble-rousing little rat”, Sowunmi added that the PRP chairman did not speak for the entire North. Asked whether he was worried that the criticism came from a Northern elder, Sowunmi said the forthcoming elections would provide a clearer indication of political support. “They can make their comments. We are going to the polls. Data would tell you that those that are the critical territorial commanders of votes, they know themselves,” he said. The convener of The Alternative also pointed to the influence of religious leaders and their followers in determining political choices, citing the case of Islamic cleric Ibrahim El-Zakzaky. He questioned whether El-Zakzaky and his followers would necessarily reject Tinubu, referring to the president’s reported provision of a private jet for the cleric to attend the funeral of his leader in Iran. Sowunmi contrasted this with the treatment El-Zakzaky and his family received from those he accused of harming them, arguing that political support could not be determined solely by the criticism of individual leaders. The post He’s a Northern kid — Sowunmi slams Baba-Ahmed for calling Tinubu ‘a failure’ appeared first on Vanguard News .
